configPages.name: Budget Configuration
configPages.verifyNotes:
ZERO FIELDS IS THE CORRECT, DELIBERATE ANSWER FOR THIS PAGE. The Budget Configuration page (/expense/admin/invoice/budgetConfiguration.asp) HAS NO DOCUMENTARY BASIS IN THIS CORPUS, and I am stating that explicitly rather than padding it.

REFUTER PAGE-LEVEL FINDINGS: the refuters returned an EMPTY findings list, and the KEEP, REPAIR and DROP lists were all empty (0/0/0), because all three extractor lenses (procedures-and-controls, tables, tools-guides-and-cross-cutting) independently emitted zero fields and zero valueSetCandidates. There was therefore nothing to keep, nothing to repair and nothing to drop. Rather than rubber-stamp a triple negative, I re-ran the search independently before accepting it.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF (not inherited from Map/Extract). Across all four directories (2230 files: 1209 admin-guides, 650 tools-guides, 138 release-notes, 233 release-note-summaries) the literal strings 'Budget Configuration', 'budgetConfiguration', 'Budget Admin', 'Budget Item', 'Budget Manager', 'Budget Viewer', 'Budget Category', 'Manage Budget', 'Budget Period', 'Budget List' and 'budget setting' each return ZERO files, case-insensitively. A nav-shape search for '> Budget' or 'Budget >' returns ZERO lines, so there is NO navigation path to record. The token '.asp' appears in ZERO files corpus-wide, so the page URL itself is unverifiable from the docs by design, not by omission. Case-insensitive 'budget' returns exactly 22 files: 16 admin-guides + 6 tools-guides + ZERO in EITHER release-note directory. That release-note silence is a real corroboration of absence and also means there is no release note to date or differentiate a UI variant, which is why uiVariant stays 'undifferentiated'. Exactly one file carries 'budget' in its name: budget-approval-59251c3b.md, 27 lines total, which I read IN FULL. It contains no procedure, no field table, no button, no nav path.

THE CORPUS DEFERS OUTWARD TO A GUIDE THAT IS NOT HERE. Four independent files point at one external deliverable, the 'Shared: Budget Setup Guide', which is NOT in this corpus (this corpus is Concur Invoice Professional Edition only, deliverable_ids 41460672 admin-guides and 41460673 tools-guides; Shared deliverables were out of scope of the 2026-08-29 crawl). Verbatim, each grep -F -c verified at count 1: budget-approval-59251c3b.md -- 'For more information about budget approval and budget workflows, refer to the _Shared: Budget Setup Guide_.' and 'Clients who use the Budget feature can set up budget approval for both invoices and purchase requests.'; approver-terminology-8559861c.md line 39 -- the same outward pointer for the Budget Approver role; add-a-custom-audit-rule-0f1d320e.md AND its gerund/imperative twin add-a-custom-audit-rule-43e3f9aa.md, both at line 154 -- 'Complete the fields. (For audit rule notifications for Budget, refer to the Shared: Budget Setup Guide.)', i.e. the corpus defers at the exact point where budget notification fields would have been enumerated. THE CONFIGURATION SURFACE OF THIS PAGE IS DOCUMENTED, JUST NOT IN THIS CORPUS. That is the deliverable for this page.

PROVISIONING FACT worth carrying to the automation: vat-at-the-line-item-level-itemization-summary-only-a41e7ad6.md states 'The Budget feature is a purchased service.' A site that has not purchased it will not surface this page at all -- consistent with the corpus never documenting its controls. This is a provisioning gate, not a configurable control, so it is not emitted as a field.

BUDGET REFERENCES I REFUSED TO RE-HOME HERE (the mis-assignment failure grep cannot catch). (a) the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md defines a Budget audit-rule DATA OBJECT -- 'Budget: Budgets associated with an invoice or purchase request' -- whose 14 operands (Actual Pending Consumption Percent, Actual Spent Consumption Percent, Alert Limit, Budget Amount, Budget Name, Budget Remaining Amount, Budget Type, Committed Pending Consumption Percent, Committed Spent Consumption Percent, Control Limit, HasBudget, Pending Consumption Percent, Period Type, Spent Consumption Percent) I read IN FULL and confirmed sit in a column of the Condition page's data-object table. They belong to page.audit-rules, ALREADY BUILT with coverage 'good'. These operand names are exactly what a plausible budget screen would be fabricated from, and that is precisely why they stay out. (b) events-triggers-72339a13.md documents the workflow event 'Payment Request Budget Submit' -- Workflows, NOT YET BUILT. (c) workflow-667cee21.md frames budget approval as a Workflow capability. (d) approver-terminology-8559861c.md defines the Budget Approver role (SAP's subject-verb error 'approvers approves' is verbatim in the source). (e) define-the-who-in-a-transaction-1488d041.md uses 'Budget Center' only as an EXAMPLE accounting segment name -- Accounting Administration, already built. (f) benefits-of-using-cost-object-approval-ed5de5de.md's 'budget ownership' is Cost Object Approval prose, not a Budget Owner role. (g) general-information-8b3b0308.md, purchase-request-and-purchase-order-8b36ae07.md and audit-rules-8b297db8.md hits are revision-history lines.

RULE 1 (BOTH DIRECTORIES WEIGHTED EQUALLY) DISCHARGED, AND IT CORRECTS THE RECON. The Map inventory listed no tools-guides files at all, but six tools-guides files do contain the token 'budget'. I opened and line-grepped every one, and all six are INCIDENTAL COMMON-NOUN PROSE, not the Budget feature: create-and-manage-allocation-favorites-22cb2e7c and -4d3a7e54 ('budget the expense', a verb); distribute-allocate-a-purchase-request-689dbc62 ('managing departmental budgets'); select-for-different-vendors-and-project-and-event-based-requests-1f3c9d5b ('budget appropriate'); understand-conditional-expressions-db3d7418 ('EuropeBudget', an invented example group name inside an audit-rule expression); workflow-and-approval-routing-8b4ff6c9 ('budget insight', Workflows routing advice). None yields a field, a value or a role gate for this page. The tools-guides skew this lens exists to correct genuinely has nothing to contribute here -- which is itself a publishable finding.

RULE 2 AND RULE 3 DISCHARGED. Raw <table> census is ZERO across all 22 budget-bearing files, so no raw-HTML catalog was missed and no fromRawHtmlTable flag could be wrong. No long catalog belongs to this page; the only enumeration in the vicinity is the 14-operand Budget data object, which I read complete and un-truncated and then assigned to Audit Rules where it belongs. Nothing was sampled or summarised.

MUST-READ: the must-read list was empty by design and I did not manufacture a reading list; mustReadSkipped is therefore empty. I did read both ALSO RELEVANT files (budget-approval-59251c3b.md in full, approver-terminology-8559861c.md at the Budget Approver bullet) plus every other budget-bearing file in the corpus.

NO SPLITS PROPOSED: a split requires a control to split, and there are none.

WHAT I COULD NOT DETERMINE: everything about this page's actual controls -- whether it has budget name, budget type, period type, control/alert limit, or owner fields; whether the Condition-page operand names mirror on-page field labels (plausible, and therefore forbidden to assume); what roles gate it; and where it hangs in the nav tree.

RECOMMENDATION TO THE MERGE: keep page.budget-configuration ONLY as an explicit zero-field 'documented elsewhere' marker naming the Shared: Budget Setup Guide, or omit the node entirely. Either is defensible; the marker is more useful because it tells a future config writer immediately WHERE to look instead of leaving them to re-run this search. Under no circumstances should a later pass synthesise a plausible budget-configuration screen from the Audit Rules operand list. coverage='thin' and THIN STAYS THIN.
configPages.identityNotes: NO DOCUMENTARY BASIS IN THIS CORPUS. THIN WITH ZERO FIELDS AND ZERO NAV PATHS IS THE CORRECT ANSWER. Exhaustive searches across BOTH guide directories and BOTH release-note directories returned zero hits for every one of: 'Budget Configuration', 'budgetConfiguration', 'Budget Admin', 'Budget Item', 'Budget Manager', 'Budget Viewer', 'Budget Owner', 'Budget Category', 'Manage Budget'. Only one file has 'budget' in its name (budget-approval-59251c3b.md) and it defers outward: 'For more information about budget approval and budget workflows, refer to the _Shared: Budget Setup Guide_.' THE CORPUS DEFERS TO THE EXTERNAL 'Shared: Budget Setup Guide', WHICH IS NOT IN THIS CORPUS (this corpus is Concur Invoice Professional Edition only). The same deferral repeats in approver-terminology-8559861c.md (Budget Approver) and in both copies of add-a-custom-audit-rule-*.md ('For audit rule notifications for Budget, refer to the Shared: Budget Setup Guide.'). Every other Budget mention belongs to an already-built or not-yet-built OTHER page and must NOT be re-homed here: (a) the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md lists a Budget audit-rule DATA OBJECT with Budget Amount / Budget Name / Budget Remaining Amount / Budget Type / HasBudget - these are Audit Rules condition operands, already built; (b) events-triggers-72339a13.md documents a 'Payment Request Budget Submit' workflow event - belongs to Workflows, not yet built; (c) approver-terminology-8559861c.md defines a Budget Approver role; (d) define-the-who-in-a-transaction-1488d041.md uses 'Budget Center' only as an example accounting segment name. configPages.verifyNotes:
INPUTS 51 (23 keep + 28 repair) -> 27 records out, 24 repair-bucket inputs moved to dropped, 0 records created. The 14 refuter-agreed drops are also recorded in 'dropped', so the array holds 38 auditable entries and every one of the 65 original candidates is accounted for. No record was split; splitsProposed is empty because nothing in the documentation shows one input to be genuinely several controls that is not already modelled as separate records (importButton vs importSubmitButton, removeConfirmation vs removeConfirmYesButton, shipToTab vs billToTab were all already split by the extractors). Refuter 2 explicitly judged the one plausible candidate - one Save serving both the Add New and Modify Ship To Location modals - to be the documented reading rather than two controls, and I did not override that.

GROUNDING RE-VERIFIED MECHANICALLY: I re-ran grep -F -c on all 27 emitted sourceQuotes against their cited files. All 27 returned exactly 1. No sourceFile carries the bad CONCUR_INVOICE/ prefix (asserted in the build script). Every quote I hand-typed into a repaired record's notes was grep-verified too: 'Add one or more shipping addresses by clicking Ship To and then New.' (=1, set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md), 'Select Yes to remove the address from the Company Locations page.' (=1), 'Select Remove. The following confirmation message appears:' (=1), 'Select the address or addresses.' (=1), 'Select the file and then select Open.' (=1), 'Select Browse and locate the file that you want to import.' (=1), 'This is only applicable on the bill-to address and required by some European countries.' (=1). Kept records were pulled programmatically out of the three extraction JSONs with python3 - nothing was retyped. VARIANT SELECTION: both refuters set verbatimVariantIndex 0 everywhere and every per-lens variant verified, so selection turned on content, not verbatimness. For the nine procedural buttons I took the unnumbered quote form the refuters themselves cited (procedure lens) rather than the crosscut lens's numbered-list form ('2.  Select New...'), which is verbatim but carries a markdown list marker into the quote; for modifyButton and downloadImportTemplateLink the two lenses share an identical quote, so I took the crosscut record for its strictly richer notes. For the 12-row address form I took the tables-lens records, which carry the row index and quote the in-cell Note/Tip; addressCode came from the crosscut lens, whose notes enumerate all three integrations (PO import External ID, Employee Import 360 default shipping, Peppol).

NO INVENTED VALUES: every emitted record has validValues [] - verified programmatically. The two populated value lists in the candidate set ('210' and '220') left with the PO-import rows, and companyLocationTab's ['Ship To','Bill To'] left with that duplicate. Nobody completed a No/Yes pair: addAddressAsShipToLocationAsWell documents only the enabled behaviour and the cleared behaviour stays unrecorded; removeConfirmation records only the affirmative Yes and I have explicitly written into its notes that the negative/Cancel control must NOT be invented. countryCode stays fieldType 'unknown' with empty values and is NOT wired to the 249-row catalog in country-code-list-8b3e2eda.md, whose documented scope is 'the country code list that you use when creating the vendor import file' - a different import. stateProvince likewise stays 'unknown' with no values: the only hint of a list is a revision-history line, which is dating evidence, not a documented enumeration. fromRawHtmlTable is false on all 27 and is justified - grep -c '<table' = 0 on every cited file.

REPAIRS ACTUALLY PERFORMED (4). (1) shipToTab and (2) billToTab: the crosscut lens typed both tabs 'button'; set to 'unknown' per the graph's settled tab convention (capture_processing_admin_tabs, scanConfigurationsTab, imagingTabSelector, validationsTab, connectedListsTab), and the corroborating admin-guides sentence plus the per-tab field-set difference (VAT ID is bill-to only) folded into notes so nothing from companyLocationTab's drop is lost. (3) removeConfirmation: was typed 'button' and labelled with the text of a confirmation MESSAGE, which would send an automation hunting for a button that does not exist; fieldType is now 'unknown', the label now says '(confirmation message)', and the notes state that the only documented control inside the dialog is Yes and that the negative half must not be completed. (4) openButton: refuters split keep/drop - refuter 1 kept it, refuter 2 argued it is the operating-system file chooser and a phantom page button is a crawler stall point. Repaired rather than deleted, because this roster has no configSteps array to demote the step into and dropping would lose a verbatim-grounded step of the page's own numbered procedure; its notes now carry the OS-dialog scope as a first-class warning telling an automation to set the file input directly. Both refuter positions are recorded on the record.

THE BIG CALL - 22 PO-IMPORT COLUMNS DROPPED, RESOLVING A DIRECT REFUTER SPLIT. Refuter 1 (grounding) kept all of poImport210BillTo_* and poImport220ShipTo_* on the argument that no PO Import page exists and rule 2 protects long catalogs. Refuter 2 (page ownership) dropped all 22 with affirmative evidence. I re-ran the decisive check myself: grep -c 'Company Locations' returns 0 in BOTH concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-bill-to-address-record-type-210-format-b8e18edd.md and .../purchase-order-ship-to-address-record-type-220-format-d6da48d9.md. I resolved in favour of refuter 2. Reasoning: rule 2 forbids sampling or truncating a catalog you are extracting - it does not license homing a complete catalog on the wrong page; the records self-refute, their own notes opening 'NOT A CONTROL ON THE COMPANY LOCATIONS PAGE'; and the harm is concrete rather than theoretical, because Company Locations has its OWN import template whose column list is documented nowhere in this corpus, so 22 import columns sitting under this page node would be read as that template's columns. Mis-assignment to the wrong page is exactly the defect grep cannot catch, which is why this pass exists. THE CATALOG IS NOT LOST: both source files are named, all 11 rows of each survive intact in extract-company-locations-tables.json, each dropped entry records its own Definition and Required? value, and the three contradictions the rows anchor travel with them - (a) Name is Required on this page but Required? = N in both 210 and 220, (b) State/Province is Optional here but Required? = Y in both, (c) Country Code is defined as '2 characters' in the 210 and 'Maximum 2 characters' in the 220. Two further re-home instructions are recorded: the literal backslash in 'future\_use' must not be cleaned up, and both futureUse rows carry fieldType 'table' which should become 'unknown' (that was refuter 1's named type defect, preserved rather than discarded). The page keeps the relationship as a dependency on addressCode: 'Identical records are those that share the same Address Code (in Company Locations) and External ID (within the associated record in the PO import).'

SECOND SPLIT RESOLVED - THE TWO ADDRESS SEARCH FIELDS DROPPED. Refuter 1 could neither confirm nor refute page ownership and routed shipToAddressSearch and billToAddressSearch to repair-with-a-flag; refuter 2 produced affirmative counter-evidence. I verified it: grep -c 'Company Locations' = 0 in the source topic search-for-a-ship-to-or-bill-to-address-1d864cfe.md, while complete-the-purchase-request-3dfd5f5c.md (grep -F -c = 1) and change-ship-to-address-564e516a.md (grep -F -c = 1) both place these labels on the end-user purchase request/order. Behavioural tells agree - you type a company NAME to pick an address and the type-ahead shows the DEFAULT address, a per-user concept meaningless when administering the master list - and none of this page's six procedures mentions a search box. A flagged field is still a field in the graph, so I dropped rather than repaired. Refuter 1 also caught an independent defect on billToAddressSearch worth preserving in the audit trail: its quote was verbatim but lifted from an adjacent passage and never named the control. Nothing useful is lost - the search-by-Name constraint already lives on locationName ('The system searches for your location by using the Name value.').

NAME HYGIENE: no two emitted records share a name (asserted in the build script). Checked against the existing graph's 330 field names: newButton, saveButton, modifyButton and removeButton already exist as field.exceptions.newbutton / savebutton / modifybutton / removebutton, but ids are page-namespaced and both sets are independently documented on their own pages, so these are distinct real controls sharing generic labels - do NOT dedupe across pages. None of my other 23 names occurs anywhere in the graph. One further confirmation that the bare 'name' spelling was correctly dropped in favour of locationName: field.policies.name already exists and means something else.

MERGE ACTIONS REQUIRED DOWNSTREAM, or things will dangle silently. (1) DELETE the tables lens's configValueSet with appliesToField 'companyLocationTab' (values Ship To / Bill To) - its target is dropped and the pair survives as the two tab records; do not re-wire it. (2) RETARGET to locationName the four dependencies aimed at the dropped spellings: two from the procedure lens (Profile > Invoice Preferences > Default Shipping Address, and User Administration > Invoice Preferences) and two from the crosscut lens (Profile default shipping address, and Bill To @ Policies). (3) DROP the dependencies routed out of shipToTab by the crosscut lens (-> Country @ Tax Administration, -> Default Shipping Address @ Tax Validation) or retarget them to countryCode / stateProvince / locationName as the tables lens does - a tab is a poor dependency source. (4) The 249-row country-code catalog should not be parented to this page at all; it belongs to whichever page owns the VENDOR import. (5) Dependencies aimed at addressCode, countryCode, stateProvince, emailAddress and locationName all survive and need no work.

CORRECTION TO THE MAP, CONFIRMED BY BOTH REFUTERS AND WORTH FIXING UPSTREAM: deliverable_id 41460673 is the entire Concur Invoice Professional Edition Tools Guides book, not a Company Locations grouping key - the three end-user purchase-request change-address topics carry the same id. It must not be used as evidence that a topic belongs to this page.

PUBLISHABLE NEGATIVE FINDINGS CARRIED FORWARD. (a) The Company Locations import template's own COLUMN LIST is documented nowhere in either guide directory - import-shipping-or-billing-addresses-601c2549.md says only that the template arrives with 'the field names already filled in'. Thin is the correct answer; it must NOT be backfilled from the 210/220 record formats, which are a different import. This is recorded on downloadImportTemplateLink. (b) No export column layout is documented either, and Export All is the only export control attested - no filtered export exists in the corpus. (c) The address list/grid's COLUMNS are never enumerated. (d) The corpus is internally inconsistent about the import surface, calling it 'the Import Ship To Locations window' at step 2 and 'the Import Ship To Locations page' at step 7; importSubmitButton and importSummaryCloseButton therefore sit one and two modal layers deep and are flattened onto this page per existing graph precedent (page.forms-and-fields 'Modify Form Fields window'). No second page node should be spawned. (e) Soft-delete semantics are a real automation constraint and survive on removeButton: 'The address remains available and can be reactivated by entering the same Address Code. The system creates a new record.'

CONTROLS THE THREE LENSES MISSED - not emitted, because creating records during Repair bypasses the adversarial refuters, but flagged for a top-up pass: (1) row selection on the address list, 'Select the address or addresses.' (delete-a-shipping-or-billing-address-ae7aef28.md, verified =1; precedent exists as page.exceptions exceptionRowCheckbox); (2) the address list/grid itself, 'The new address appears as a row on the Company Locations page.'; (3) the 'Ship To Locations import history' section named in 601c2549; (4) the down-arrow alternative on the address picker in f772bed1, which carries the same end-user-surface ownership doubt that removed the two search fields and should not be added without resolving it.

QUOTE-AMBIGUITY WARNING FOR ANY FUTURE RE-VALIDATION: the strings 'Address 1 of the complete address.', 'The city within which the address resides.', 'The postal code of the address.', 'The state or province within which the address resides.' and 'The code of the country associated with the address.' are byte-identical between this page's field table and both PO import record tables. sourceFile is the only thing separating a page field from an import column; matching on quote text alone will conflate them.

MUST-READ COVERAGE: nothing skipped for my lens. I worked from both refuters' full reads and independently re-read or re-grepped the decisive files: add-a-shipping-or-billing-address-3b51c816.md (the 12-row catalog, complete - all 12 rows are present as locationName, addressCode, address1-3, city, postalCode, countryCode, stateProvince, emailAddress, vatId and the check box), the delete/edit/import/export procedures, the two PO import record formats (grep -c 'Company Locations' = 0 on both), search-for-a-ship-to-or-bill-to-address-1d864cfe.md, complete-the-purchase-request-3dfd5f5c.md, change-ship-to-address-564e516a.md and set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md. country-code-list-8b3e2eda.md (2336 lines) was not read row-by-row in this pass: its 249 rows are deliberately not this page's validValues, both refuters verified the row count and the scope sentence mechanically, and re-reading it could not change any disposition here.

COVERAGE JUDGEMENT 'good': the corpus documents this page at field level with a complete 12-row field table plus nine attested action controls, two tabs and a confirmation dialog, and both refuters found zero grounding defects across 91 variant records. The gaps that remain (import template columns, export layout, grid columns, the cleared state of the check box, the negative confirmation control) are genuine documentation gaps, recorded rather than filled.

I adopted refuter 2's long-form convention for the ENTIRE set, which is exactly the inversion refuter 1 authorised ('If refuter 2 nominates the long-form names instead, invert the whole set consistently - but NEVER delete both halves of a pair'). 3. WHERE THE DROPPED HALF WAS THE BETTER RECORD, I TOOK ITS CONTENT. That is the whole point of a three-way disposition. Nine quotes were replaced with the better-anchored or fuller sentence FROM THE SAME FILE and re-verified: taxAuthoritiesGridStateProvince, taxAuthoritiesGridTaxName, taxRateTaxPercent, taxValidationPartnerAccountNumber, taxValidationType, taxValidationExpenseTypes, expenseTypeGroupTaxCode, expenseTypeGroupRateTypeColumn, vendorGroupTaxCode, vendorGroupDisableVatCalculation. 'Select the Payment Request document type for which to calculate VAT...' is prose naming one document type, not an enumerated option list, and I confirmed by grep that 'Applies To' appears in exactly two tax files corpus-wide (step-5 and step-6) and is never enumerated in either. configPages.verifyNotes: ASSEMBLED PROGRAMMATICALLY FROM THE THREE EXTRACTION FILES (python3, no retyping); only the nine repaired records were hand-authored, and every sourceQuote in the roster - carried or hand-authored - was re-verified mechanically against ROOT/<sourceFile> with a str.count containment check equivalent to grep -F -c. GROUNDING. Both refuters ran an exact-substring pass over all 228 lens records and agreed: 228/228 sourceQuotes verbatim, 228/228 cited files present, zero CONCUR_INVOICE/ path regressions. I re-ran that check myself before assembly (228/228) and again on the 114 emitted records after every edit: 114/114 verbatim, 0 path defects, 0 duplicate names. Every quote I hand-authored during repair was grep -F -c'd against its cited file first; all returned 1.

ASSEMBLY METHOD. Records were pulled programmatically out of the three lens JSONs - no quote was retyped. 28 names existed in two lens files under the SAME name; for those I emitted one record (the first lens in the refuters' foundByLenses order, i.e. verbatimVariantIndex 0) and appended the other lens's notes to it verbatim so nothing observed was lost. Two of those variant choices were made against index 0 on explicit refuter instruction: cost_object_hierarchy_type takes the crosscut quote from step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md because the procedures quote was a value bullet naming no field, and steps_can_be_added_by takes the crosscut record because it is the only one whose cited file enumerates the values.

COUNTS. 96 keeps carried through, 18 routed to repair, 17 of them actually changed; step_email_employee_when_step_is_complete was routed to repair only because the second refuter returned no verdict (a missing verdict routes to Repair, never to deletion) - I re-read work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md, found row 7 sound and its quote verbatim, and changed nothing but the audit note. 86 dropped, every one a duplication drop naming its survivor; NOT ONE control was dropped for failing to be a control, and nothing was dropped for thinness. 114 in, 114 out.

WHAT I REPAIRED, BY CLASS. (a) Six quotes that were verbatim but anchored no control - bare value strings or a truncated NBSP nav fragment - replaced with a field-level sentence from the SAME cited file: expiration_email_to_approver, assignment_timeout_action, restrict_authorized_approver_for, email_notifications_field, allow_employee_to_automatically_transmit_purchase_orders, consolidate_pr_items_same_vendor_into_single_po, plus email_notif_find_workflow_emails_where and step_rule_send_back_message. (b) ONE WRONG-ROW QUOTE, the only defect on this page a grep gate cannot see: workflow_condition_operator_d quoted the E: Data Object row's text. Replaced with the D: Operator row's own line. Note for the builder: columns C and F genuinely share byte-identical row text in the source - that is what the corpus says, not an extractor error. (c) Value-set defects: step_approver_editable_by and step_deletable_by carried the prose article ('the employee' -> 'employee'), with the honest caveat that this enumeration is inline prose the corpus never renders as a list; confirmation_agreement_text had the eight allowed HTML FORMATTING TAGS sitting in validValues, which is markup permitted inside a free-text field and not selectable values - emptied, tags kept in notes with the source's own lower-case '<u>' preserved, 2000-character limit retained as the real constraint. (d) settings_prevent_payment_request_submission_exception_level was the one control whose every available quote carried raw HTML ('...exceeds <cite class="cite">X</cite>'); its label now holds the rendered text and its quote is the same packed cell's description 'Type a number from one to 99.' fromRawHtmlTable stays true. (e) step_rule_exception_visibility kept, fieldType 'unknown', but flagged in notes as a CROSS-SURFACE REFERENCE rather than independent evidence of a third instance - four Audit Rules files define the field, this Workflows file only references it in the Generate Exception context.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. (1) NO SPLITS. add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md documents Email Subject and Email Body twice each, once on the Primary Recipient step and once on the Delegate Recipient step (the delegate body additionally gated by the Use Primary Recipient Email check box) - genuinely two controls apiece. Records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuter, so both stay single records and the splits are reported in splitsProposed for a human. (2) NO RENAMES. One refuter asked for remove_workflow_step -> btn_remove_workflow_step and for email_notif_find_workflow_emails_where -> email_notification_find_workflow_emails_where; both are reasonable family-consistency fixes, but a rename introduces a name the refuters never judged, so both are recorded in the records' notes and here instead. (3) NO RECONCILIATION of the four contradictions this page carries into the graph: the Email Notifications granularity split (one multiselect in 554e86aa vs three per-slot fields in 663bb8ac - both kept); the Steps Can Be Added By value wording (554e86aa's 'the employee and/or the approver' implies an option b847d65b's two-value list omits - list NOT treated as exhaustive); the invoice/payment-request LABEL DRIFT on two Settings-tab controls (general-information-8b3b0308.md says 'Filter invoice items...' and 'Allow processor to recall an invoice...', invoice-settings-cace748d.md says 'payment request' - BOTH forms are kept in notes because a label-matching driver fails against a tenant rendering the other); and the 'Type a number from one to 99.' range in all three settings files against the built Exceptions page's '0 and 99', recorded as a genuine cross-page discrepancy.

NAMING RULE HONOURED. All nine Settings-tab controls are emitted under settings_* and the invoice_settings_* / pr_settings_* / po_settings_* spellings are dropped. Naming any of these 'Invoice Settings' would merge Workflows > Settings tab with the BUILT Invoice Settings page, whose 13 fields come from entirely different files; both refuters re-verified against the 486-field graph that ZERO existing fields cite invoice-settings-cace748d.md, purchase-request-settings-b0bce285.md, purchase-order-settings-a5a997b4.md or conditional-expressions-and-the-condition-page-4d98af34.md. NOTHING MOVES OFF THE BUILT PAGE. Likewise the condition editor was deduped ON FILES, never on the built Audit Rules field list (which is itself internally duplicated ~8 times); the workflow_condition_* prefix is what stops this run from propagating that error.

ENDPOINTS RESOLVED BY THIS ROSTER: dep.g1.021 'workflow deletion' -> btn_remove_workflow; dep.g2.012 -> settings_prevent_purchase_request_submission_exception_level; dep.g2.013 -> settings_prevent_purchase_order_transmission_exception_level; dep.g2ar.024 / dep.g2ar.026 'exception_level_limit' -> minimum_exception_level / maximum_exception_level (both on Authorized Approvers > Configuration, and note the corpus documents NO numeric range for them - none was invented).

EXISTING-GRAPH DEFECTS TO REPORT, NOT FIXED HERE: (1) dep.g2.011 targets page 'Invoice Settings' while citing invoice-settings-cace748d.md; it should target Workflows > Settings tab. (2) dep.g2ar.025 targets 'Invoice Settings' on a quote naming Workflows and Settings and duplicates dep.g2ar.024. (3) page.exceptions.navPathAlternates contains 'Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Settings', a route to the Settings tab and not to Exceptions. (4) The map phase found the recon's Approval-Statuses sub-tab citation was actually a Delegate Configurations quote; the correct citation is adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md. (5) Two probable G1 gaps found while ruling scope: prevent-approver-from-adding-and-deleting-line-items-in-an-invoice-9de9dba8.md and prevent-processor-to-change-vendor-pending-processor-in-workflow-edbca7d1.md both say explicitly 'On the Invoice Settings page' and are cited by zero graph nodes - report against the BUILT page, do NOT home them on Workflows.

uiVariant = 'undifferentiated', AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER, NOT A HEDGE. No *-new-experience-* twin exists for any workflow file. Two dated statements in one corpus version point opposite ways: general-information-8b3b0308.md, dated September 19 2025, logs 'Updated images and text to the new UI for the Workflows Tool' (carrying the once-corpus-wide typo 'Worflows'), which makes the missing twin a replacement revised in place rather than a coverage gap; while tools-guides/how-single-step-approval-workflow-works-40145f24.md says the administrator 'uses the Authorized Approvers link from workflows in the classic interface'. THE CORPUS CANNOT SETTLE WHICH UI GENERATION THE CLICK PATHS DESCRIBE. This matters more than any single field on this page: navigation is the only knowledge here a driver cannot re-derive at runtime, so if the paths describe a superseded UI every navPath is wrong at once. (4) cost_object_approval_level - CONTESTED EXISTENCE BURIED IN PROSE. Refuter 2 asked for a field-level contested marker. Recorded as strengthening the two-values-one-label HYPOTHESIS, never as a resolution. The contradiction stays open.
(5) approval_limit_currency_branch_a - ONE NON-VERBATIM CHARACTER in a notes quote: a trailing period the source does not have. configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to allow users to edit the amounts in the Amount column.
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page.

configFields.name: Allow users to enter the count of "No Shows"
configFields.label: Allow users to enter the count of "No Shows"
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to allow users to account for "No Shows," that is attendees who were invited but did not attend.
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page. Casing of 'No Shows' varies between topics.

configFields.name: Allow users to edit the count of attendees
configFields.label: Allow users to edit the count of attendees
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to allow users to enter a count (number of unnamed attendees) for this expense type.
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page. Used in conjunction with attendee type settings.

configFields.name: Include user as an attendee by default
configFields.label: Include user as an attendee by default
configFields.sourceQuote: If this check box is selected, Concur Invoice automatically adds the user as an attendee when the user accesses the attendees section the first time (when no attendees are assigned to the entry).
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page.

configFields.name: Display the Add New Attendees button from the attendee table
configFields.label: Display the Add New Attendees button from the attendee table
configFields.sourceQuote: If this check box is selected, Invoice adds the Add New Attendee button to the Attendee section of the Attendee tab.
configFields.notes: LABEL DRIFT -- the dedicated Policies-tool procedure names it without 'Add': 'Clear the Display the New Attendee button from the attendee table (shown in its selected, default state in the figure below).' (procedure-suppress-the-new-attendee-button-by-expense-type-9a8edae0.md, which reaches it via Administration > Invoice > Policies > select policy > Expense Types > double-click expense type). Default state is selected.

configFields.name: Group
configFields.label: Group
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the correct group as it should appear within the other tools and to the employee.
configFields.notes: First row of the "Table 1: Configuration for Group fields" table in the Add Groups topic. The value is chosen through a separate Select Group window opened by New, not typed. Available groups are constrained by the admin's rights: "You can only create group configurations for groups for which you are assigned rights and for groups below those groups." (same file).

configFields.name: Group Name
configFields.label: Group Name
configFields.sourceQuote: Type a unique name that describes this group. When creating other configurations, you will see the group name and not the group path, so make sure it is descriptive of what group is being defined.
configFields.notes: Free-text, must be unique. The Vendor Access tab equivalent adds a naming constraint: "It cannot be the name of any existing group name already in the system." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md).

configFields.name: Attendee List Form
configFields.label: Attendee List Form
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the attendee form that should be displayed when a new attendee is added.
configFields.notes: Options are the attendee forms configured in Forms and Fields (form type Payment Request Attendee Detail View) — the corpus never enumerates them, so validValues is empty. LABEL DRIFT: the same control is called the "Forms Fields list" in a second topic (see separate entry).

configFields.name: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
configFields.label: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
configFields.sourceQuote: CFDi digital invoice images are required under Mexican regulatory policies. Select (enable) this setting (cleared/disabled by default) to allow users to view the CFDi Attachment command in the Actions menu and attach a digital invoice image to their invoice.
configFields.notes: Documented as cleared/disabled by default. LABEL DRIFT (singular "user"): "Select (enable) the Allow user to upload CFDi attachments check box." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-enable-by-invoice-group-ebe8724b.md. A third topic uses the plural form again (enabling-cfdi-attachments-for-reporting-to-mexican-tax-authorities-5ce1fd0c.md).

configFields.name: Allow Invoice Owners to create invoices
configFields.label: Allow Invoice Owners to create invoices
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this setting (the default) to allow the Invoice Owner role to create an invoice in Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: Selected by default per the description. Historical label in the guide's revision history was "Allow Invoice Owners in Group to Create Payment Requests" (group-configuration-8b2ecb41.md, April 11 2014 row) — a matcher should tolerate the older wording.

configFields.name: Allow Invoice Owners to change vendors on assigned invoices
configFields.label: Allow Invoice Owners to change vendors on assigned invoices
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this setting to allow the Invoice Owner role to change the currently assigned vendor to a different vendor for any invoice assigned to the owner by the AP User.
configFields.notes: Scope note in the same table cell: "This applies only to those invoices not created by the Invoice Owner. If the owner created the invoice, they can change the vendor." Historical label "Allow Invoice Owners to Change Vendors" appears in the revision history (group-configuration-8b2ecb41.md).

configFields.name: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for
configFields.label: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for
configFields.sourceQuote: For each role, you may select an option that governs if that user is required to add banking information in the Vendor Banking Information section when requesting a new vendor.
configFields.notes: Not one control but a per-role set of selectors — one option per role. The three options ARE literally enumerated in the same table cell, so validValues is populated: "Hidden: The section does not appear, and there is nothing for the user to see or fill out." / "Required: The section appears, and all fields that must logically be filled out are marked as Required (Red highlight)." / "Optional: The section appears, but no enforcement of data entry is required unless the user fills in one or more Required fields." The corpus does not enumerate WHICH roles get a selector; it names the Invoice User and Invoice Vendor Manager roles elsewhere (concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/enabling-the-vendor-manager-to-enter-the-vendor-s-banking-information-fcb8fbdd.md).

configFields.name: Is Active for Group
configFields.label: Is Active for Group
configFields.sourceQuote: If a policy is marked as Active, it is available for inclusion into an invoice created by a member of the selected group. If a policy is marked as Inactive, it is not available.
configFields.notes: Check-box column in the Policies sub-window, one row per policy. Interaction: 'Select or clear the check box make the policy active or inactive for the new group.' (sic — verbatim, missing 'to'). Also referenced as a column heading in enable-e-bunsho-timestamp-for-a-policy-group-07ea2db1.md: 'In the Is Active for Group, check the box next to the e-Bunsho enabled policy.' policy-c8ec906b.md uses the capitalization variant 'Is Active For Group'.

configFields.name: Is Default Policy
configFields.label: Is Default Policy
configFields.sourceQuote: You will be unable to select a policy as a default if it is marked Inactive. In addition, if there is only one Active policy listed for a group, it will automatically be set to Yes in the Is Default Policy column. It cannot be changed to No until another policy available for the group is marked Active.
configFields.notes: Check-box column rendered as Yes/No in the grid. Two hard dependency rules, both structural: (1) cannot be set on a policy marked Inactive; (2) auto-forced to Yes and locked when the group has exactly one Active policy. Purpose: 'when an employee creates an invoice, the policy that appears as a default will be the one selected here.'

configFields.name: Is Inheritable
configFields.label: Is Inheritable
configFields.sourceQuote: Select or clear the check box to set whether groups below this group will inherit the group settings.
configFields.notes: Drives the hierarchy fallback: "If a group below this group does not have a configuration associated with it, and this group configuration does not allow inheritance, then when an employee creates an invoice, it will inherit policies from the group above this group rather than from this group." (same cell).

configFields.name: Policies
configFields.label: Policies (column, Modify link)
configFields.sourceQuote: Click Modify in the Policies column. The Configuration for Group window appears.
configFields.notes: Grid column on the Invoice tab whose per-row Modify link opens the policy sub-window carrying Is Active for Group / Is Default Policy / Is Inheritable. Corroborated: "On the Group Configurations page, in the Policies column, select the Modify link for a list of policies available to the group." (change-the-active-policy-d656d79c.md) and "On the Administration > Invoice > Group Configurations page in the Policies column, click Modify for the group you want to modify." (enable-e-bunsho-timestamp-for-a-policy-group-07ea2db1.md).

configFields.name: attendee type active check boxes
configFields.label: (attendee type rows in Configuration for Group)
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the check box for all attendee types that should be active for the group.
configFields.notes: One check box per attendee type inside the Attendee Types sub-window. Two structural constraints stated in the same file: "All attendee types appear except No Shows and This Employee since they are system attendee types and cannot be inactive." and "If an attendee type is set to Active at the parent group level, it will remain active at the child group level and cannot be changed to Inactive. If the attendee type is set to Inactive at the parent group level, it can be overridden at the child group level and set to Active." The set of attendee types is tenant-configured, so validValues is empty.

configFields.name: In Use
configFields.label: In Use
configFields.sourceQuote: In Use is an indicator that a group configuration is directly referred to within the overall configuration, and therefore cannot be deleted until that related configuration is updated. This does not indicate that users are assigned to the group. Some common examples of related configuration would be Company News records or conditions within Audit Rules.
configFields.notes: Read-only indicator on the list grid; gates deletability (an In Use row has no selection check box). The Group Configuration guide's revision history confirms it as a page element: "Added clarification regarding the In Use indicator." (group-configuration-8b2ecb41.md, April 22, 2022).

configFields.name: New
configFields.label: New
configFields.sourceQuote: On the Invoice tab of the Group Configurations page, select New. The Select Group window appears.
configFields.notes: Present on both tabs. Vendor Access equivalent: "Click New to open the Select Group window." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md).

configFields.name: Modify
configFields.label: Modify
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the desired group configuration and click Modify. The Configuration for Group page appears.
configFields.notes: Row-level action that opens the basic Configuration for Group window. Also used read-only for viewing: "Select Modify to view the configuration." (view-group-configurations-9e1e5066.md). Distinct from the per-column Modify links in Policies and Attendee Types.

configFields.name: Delete Selected Rows
configFields.label: Delete Selected Rows
configFields.sourceQuote: Click Delete Selected Rows.
configFields.notes: Deletes the checked group configurations. Deleting the configuration does not delete the group itself: "Although an Invoice Configuration administrator can delete a group configuration, they cannot delete the group itself. Groups are defined by the source list imported into the system." (same file).

configFields.name: Select All
configFields.label: Select All
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Select All to choose all the available group configurations. Note that not all group configurations will be available for removal as they either are in use or required by Concur Invoice. These group configurations will not have associated check boxes.
configFields.notes: Bulk-select control on the Group Configurations List page; only selects rows that actually have check boxes.

configFields.name: Vendor Access tab
configFields.label: Vendor Access
configFields.sourceQuote: Click the Vendor Access tab.
configFields.notes: Second tab. Scope: "The Vendor Access tab of Group Configurations within Invoice Processing Admin is used to create those vendor groups to which you will assign vendors via import. These groups are then assigned in turn to users via User Administration to filter what vendors a user may choose from." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/overview-8b2edfd0.md). Deep-linkable as a breadcrumb leaf (see navPathEvidence).

configFields.name: Email Alias
configFields.label: Email Alias
configFields.sourceQuote: In the Configuration for Group window, select the preferred email alias from the Email Alias list.
configFields.notes: Appears on the Vendor Access tab's Configuration for Group window, and only once Vendor Segregation is on: "Now, the functionality appears in Group Configuration > Vendor Access" (same file). Options are the aliases created in Capture Processing Admin > Email Administration, so they are tenant data and validValues stays empty.

configFields.name: Group (Vendor Access list)
configFields.label: Group
configFields.sourceQuote: In the Group list, select a vendor group, and then click Modify.
configFields.notes: Vendor group picker on the Vendor Access tab used to choose which vendor group's configuration to open. Contents are the named vendor groups created on this tab.

configFields.name: Done
configFields.label: Done
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Done. The Configuration for Group window appears.
configFields.notes: Commits the group choice in the Select Group window and advances to Configuration for Group.

configFields.name: Save
configFields.label: Save
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Save. The Group Configurations page appears.
configFields.notes: Commits the Configuration for Group window and returns to the list. Present in the basic, Policies, Attendee Types, and Vendor Access variants of the window.

configFields.name: Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf
configFields.label: Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf
configFields.sourceQuote: Select to allow the Concur Invoice user to remove images attached to invoices created by the AP User and assigned to the user. Clear (disable) to prevent the user from removing images associated with the invoice.
configFields.notes: Quote enumerates both states explicitly (Select / Clear (disable)). Default Status column in the same file: 'Enabled (selected)'. ADMIN/prevent-deletion-of-images-associated-with-an-invoice-a0521ec4.md repeats: 'The setting is selected (enabled) by default.'

configFields.name: Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles
configFields.label: Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles
configFields.sourceQuote: Select to allow a Processor to change the vendor associated with an invoice even during workflow steps pending a Processor. Clear (disable) to prevent the Processor from changing the vendor if the invoice is pending any Processor role in workflow (accounting review).
configFields.notes: Quote enumerates both states explicitly. Default Status column in the same file: 'Enabled (selected)'. ADMIN/prevent-processor-to-change-vendor-pending-processor-in-workflow-edbca7d1.md confirms: 'The setting is selected (enabled) by default.'

configFields.name: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
configFields.label: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
configFields.sourceQuote: Clear (disable) this check box to remove the Banking Import link from Payment Manager and prevent the Payment Manager role from importing any changes to banking information.
configFields.notes: Inverted-sense setting: the documented action is clearing it. Default Status column in the same file: 'Enabled (selected)'. Caution — ADMIN/prevent-changes-to-payment-manager-banking-information-4fd01601.md contains a contradiction in its prose ('If you prefer this role not have this capability, select (enable) this setting to remove the Banking Import link') while its own numbered procedure says 'clear (disable) the Allow Payment Manager to change banking information check box'. The procedure and the settings table agree; the prose sentence is an error.

configFields.name: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
configFields.label: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
configFields.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box if you want vendors to receive an email when they are paid via ACH or Check with Invoice Pay. The email will contain full remittance information including when, how, and for what they are paid.
configFields.notes: Default Status column in the same file: 'Disabled (cleared)'. Edition split worth capturing: TOOLS/email-remittance-notifications-ec277e48.md states 'For Standard Edition, this setting does not display in the UI but defaults to enabled.' Payment types covered are enumerated as Check and ACH; applies to both partial and full payments; Client Pay (payment outside Invoice Pay) does not trigger notifications.

configFields.name: Enable Peppol Integration
configFields.label: Enable Peppol Integration
configFields.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box to allow Peppol Integration and configure the feature in Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: Default Status column in the same file: 'Disabled (cleared)'. This checkbox only unlocks the feature — actual configuration happens on a separate Peppol Configuration page (Administration > Invoice > Invoice Processing Admin > Peppol Configuration, per ADMIN/professional-edition-7e36681a.md), whose own 'Peppol Integration Enablement' field is a distinct two-value selector with values Active and Inactive (ADMIN/deactivating-peppol-integration-f8577b2a.md). ADMIN/feature-activation-04b47637.md notes the feature must first be enabled by SAP Concur staff via a service request.

configFields.name: Default payment term (days)
configFields.label: Default payment term (days)
configFields.sourceQuote: On the Invoice Settings page, input a value, in days, which will become the default payment term for all invoices not otherwise given a term within Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: Default value is "Zero (0) days". Master table gives examples "10, 30, or 60 days" — illustrative, not an enumeration, so validValues left empty. Casing drifts to "Default Payment Term (Days)" in the topic title and "Default Payment Term (days)" in ADMIN/understanding-default-payment-terms-e71743f2.md. Overridable per vendor record and via Invoice Pay.

configFields.name: Default Discount Terms (days)
configFields.label: Default Discount Terms (days)
configFields.sourceQuote: If a discount applies, enter the NET discount terms agreed upon with the supplier.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". The table adds a Note: the data in this field is for information purposes only and is not used in any calculations.

configFields.name: Default discount percentage
configFields.label: Default discount percentage
configFields.sourceQuote: Enter the percentage amount (10; 15) the supplier will honor if the supplier’s discount NET terms are met.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". Master table states the data type constraint verbatim: "Number (11, 8) - 11 characters maximum, 8 characters maximum to the right of the decimal." Informational only, not used in calculations. Quote contains U+2019 in supplier’s.

configFields.name: Default shipping method
configFields.label: Default shipping method
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the preferred carrier for shipping. This is designated by a code representing the shipping method used by the supplier.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". Typed as a dropdown because the corpus verb is "Select" and the value is a code; the option list is NOT enumerated anywhere in the corpus.

configFields.name: Default shipping terms
configFields.label: Default shipping terms
configFields.sourceQuote: The code representing shipping terms with a supplier.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". The corpus gives no verb (no select or enter) for this control, so the widget type cannot be determined from 2026_08 text — marked unknown rather than guessed.

configFields.name: Default recurring Invoice Generation Offset
configFields.label: Default Recurring Invoice Generation Offset
configFields.sourceQuote: Use the Default Recurring Invoice Generation Offset field on the Invoice Settings page to set the number of days before the payment date that Concur Invoice automatically generates recurring invoices. The default offset is 14 days.
configFields.notes: Default value is 14 (days). Master table writes it with lowercase r as "Default recurring Invoice Generation Offset"; the dedicated topic title-cases it. Number of days before the actual billing/payment date the recurring invoice is generated.

configFields.name: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
configFields.label: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
configFields.sourceQuote: Use the Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices list on the Invoice Settings page to select which invoice attributes are checked alongside Vendor when the Is Duplicate audit rule runs in Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: validValues are genuinely enumerated in this file: "Available fields are: Invoice Date / Invoice Amount / Invoice Number". Vendor is always checked and is not a selectable option. Default selection is Invoice Number (master table Default Status column). Multi-select — the file notes that to use more than one option the admin must use an AND statement when creating the Is Duplicate audit rule, and that an Is Duplicate rule must also be created in the Audit Rules tool.

configFields.name: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
configFields.label: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
validValues: From the associated purchase order line
configFields.sourceQuote: Use the For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied? setting on the Invoice Settings page to control whether allocation fields on invoice lines are copied from the associated purchase order line or from the existing copy-down configuration.
configFields.notes: Both options are literally enumerated as a bulleted list in this file and again in the master table. Default is "From the associated purchase order line". ADMIN/copy-down-of-po-allocation-lines-f14c45e4.md renders the second option without the hyphen as "From the copydown configurations" — tolerate both spellings. The corpus calls it a list, hence dropdown.

configFields.name: search_routing_mappings
configFields.label: Search Routing Mappings
configFields.sourceQuote: input the search criteria into the Search Routing Mappings search box as follows:
configFields.notes: Search box on the Hierarchy Mapping List screen; accepts Employee Last Name or Segment 1-3 criteria (see related fields).

configFields.name: employee_last_name
configFields.label: Employee Last Name
configFields.sourceQuote: Employee Last Name: Type the last name of the employee who is associated with the hierarchy mapping that you want to display. For example, if Ken Brown is associated with the mapping, type "Brown" in the Begins With search field.
configFields.notes: One of the search criteria options within Search Routing Mappings; uses a Begins With match.

configFields.name: segment_1_3
configFields.label: Segment 1 - 3
configFields.sourceQuote: Segment 1 - 3: You can elect to search for the mapping by typing in any of the first three segments mappings. For example, if the mapping is Company > Sales > North, and you only remember North, select the correct sequence (Segment 3 in this example) and input North in the Begins With search field.
configFields.notes: Search by any of the first three hierarchy path segments; requires selecting the matching segment sequence.

configFields.name: delete_flag
configFields.label: Delete?
configFields.sourceQuote: Used to indicate if this record should be deleted from the hierarchy mapping list.
configFields.notes: Import template field, 1 character, Y (Yes) or N (No), not required.

configFields.name: employee_id
configFields.label: Employee ID
configFields.sourceQuote: The exact Employee ID of the employee to whom the record is to be assigned.
configFields.notes: Import template field, required unless Delete? is used; max 48 characters, case insensitive.

configFields.name: level_1_10_code
configFields.label: Level 1 Code - Level 10 Code
configFields.sourceQuote: The hierarchy path, in levels (segments) on selection of which will cause the associated user in Employee ID to be selected as the default Invoice owner when the AP user assigns the invoice.
configFields.notes: Import template fields Level 1 Code through Level 10 Code; max 32 characters, case insensitive; values are List Item Short Codes.

configFields.name: browse_button
configFields.label: Browse
configFields.sourceQuote: On the Import Hierarchy Mappings page, click Browse.
configFields.notes: File-picker trigger on the Import Hierarchy Mappings tab to select the populated template file.

configFields.name: import_button
configFields.label: Import
configFields.sourceQuote: Click Import.
configFields.notes: Submits the uploaded file; triggers the Import Summary window.

configFields.name: download_template_button
configFields.label: Download Template
configFields.sourceQuote: On the Import Hierarchy Mappings page, click Download Template.
configFields.notes: Downloads the pre-populated Excel template with correct column headings.

configFields.name: import_details_type_filter
configFields.label: Type
configFields.sourceQuote:
you can filter the information that displays using the Type list that includes the following options:

-   All: The error, warning, and information text all appear
    
-   Error: Filters to display only the errors generated during import
    
-   Warning: Filters to display only the warnings generated during import
    
-   Info: Filters to display only the number of records imported
configFields.notes: Filter dropdown in the Import Details window, reached via View Import Details action.

configFields.name: exceptionCode
configFields.label: Exception Code
configFields.sourceQuote: Type a unique one to eight alphanumeric character code in all capital letters, without any spaces. This code is determined by the client's internal coding system and is not localized. Using the Exception Code, an invoice can be queried in Invoice Processor using a custom query.
configFields.notes: Required field on the New Exception tab. Unique 1-8 alphanumeric chars, all caps, no spaces. Not localized.

configFields.name: message
configFields.label: Message
configFields.sourceQuote: This message appears wherever the exception is visible and can be localized.
configFields.notes: The exception's display/description text; localizable.

configFields.name: editableByGroups
configFields.label: Editable By Group(s)
configFields.sourceQuote: If you select Global Group, then the exception can be edited or deleted by any employee assigned to administer the Global Group.
configFields.notes: Only 'Global Group' is a named fixed option in the text; all other selectable values are the client's own hierarchy group names (e.g. 'Global Group>United States'), not a corpus-enumerated set — omitted per rule 6/5. Corrected 2026-08-31: fromRawHtmlTable flag cleared — the cited file contains no <table> element. The value came from a markdown pipe table.

configFields.name: newButton
configFields.label: New
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Exceptions  New.
configFields.notes: Opens the New Exception tab. Note: 'If the administrator does not have permissions, the New link does not appear.'

configFields.name: saveButton
configFields.label: Save
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Save.
configFields.notes: Commits the new or modified exception; result note: 'The Exceptions page appears with the new exception listed.'

configFields.name: modifyButton
configFields.label: Modify
configFields.sourceQuote: Choose Modify to open the Modify Exception window.
configFields.notes: Opens the Modify Exception window for the selected exception row; read-only if the admin lacks create rights.

configFields.name: removeButton
configFields.label: Remove
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Remove.
configFields.notes: Deletes the checked exception row(s); Group admins can only remove exceptions they created, only Global admins can delete/modify all ('If you are a Group Invoice Configuration Administrator, you cannot delete exceptions that you have not created. Only Global Invoice Configuration Administrators can delete or modify all exceptions.').

configFields.name: exceptionRowCheckbox
configFields.label: (row selection checkbox)
configFields.sourceQuote: select the check box beside the desired exception
configFields.notes: Per-row checkbox on the Exceptions list used before Remove.

configFields.name: task_def_name
configFields.label: Task Def Name
configFields.sourceQuote: Task Def Name: The name of the task.
configFields.notes: Field appears on Verification, Content Extraction, Document Separation, and Automated Document Separation task-definition rows in Modify Task Definition window.

configFields.name: verification_header_form
configFields.label: Header (Verification forms)
configFields.sourceQuote: Header: Specify the header form to use
configFields.notes: One of three form selectors under Verification task definition; forms are configured via the Forms and Fields tab.

configFields.name: verification_line_item_form
configFields.label: Line Item (Verification forms)
configFields.sourceQuote: Line Item: Specify the line item form to use

configFields.name: verification_vendor_form
configFields.label: Vendor (Verification forms)
configFields.sourceQuote: Vendor: Specify the vendor form to use

configFields.name: disable_task_definition_verification
configFields.label: Disable Task Definition (Verification)
configFields.sourceQuote: Disable Task Definition: No (enabled) by default; select Yes (disabled) to disable verification.
configFields.notes: Same-named control repeats per task with task-specific default (see Automated Document Separation, default Yes).

configFields.name: instruction_text
configFields.label: Instruction Text
configFields.sourceQuote: Instruction Text: For more information, refer to Configuring: Exception Email Address and Instruction Text Options in this document.
configFields.notes: Lives under Verification task definition (Modify Task Definition window), not the Other Settings tab, per revision history: "The Instruction Text and Capture Attention To task settings are moved to the Task Definitions tab, under the Verification task definition."

configFields.name: capture_attention_to
configFields.label: Capture Attention To
configFields.sourceQuote: By setting this option to Yes (default is No), Capture Processing will attempt to capture the name and route accordingly.
configFields.notes: Adds the optional "Assign Invoice To" field to the Invoice Details section of the Verification tab when enabled. Disable when Routing Configuration auto-routing is used.

configFields.name: disable_task_definition_content_extraction
configFields.label: Disable Task Definition (Content Extraction)
configFields.sourceQuote: Disable Task Definition: No (enabled) by default; select Yes (disabled) to disable content extraction.

configFields.name: default_language
configFields.label: Default Language
configFields.sourceQuote: Default Language: Set the default language used on extraction.
configFields.notes: Content Extraction task definition field.

configFields.name: disable_task_definition_doc_separation
configFields.label: Disable Task Definition (Document Separation)
configFields.sourceQuote: Disable Task Definition: No (enabled) by default; select Yes (disabled) in conjunction with selecting No in the Automated Document Separation definition to have the system perform automated (not manual) separation of document pages to processing-ready state.

configFields.name: task_definitions_edit_button
configFields.label: Edit (Task Definitions list)
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the definition and click Edit.
configFields.notes: List-level control opening the Modify Task Definition window.

configFields.name: add_email_address

The tool includes options available on several tabs on the page:

-   Task Definition: Specify the forms (if required) for the verification task and configure separation and extraction tasks.

-   Other Settings: Additional settings for configuration of Capture Processing
configFields.notes: Canonical 5-tab catalog for the Capture Processing Admin page; all five validValues are now anchored by the quote itself. ALIAS: this bullet writes the second tab as 'Task Definition' (singular), while working-with-options-on-the-task-definitions-tab-735ce2d9.md and accessing-capture-processing-admin-2fb515a6.md write it plural — 'Task Definitions in the Task Definitions tab...', 'In Capture Processing, click the Task Definitions tab.' Same tab, both spellings in the 2026_08 corpus. LANDING STATE: per accessing-capture-processing-admin-2fb515a6.md, 'The page opens to the Capture Processing view of the Forms and Fields tab.' ORDERING/PREREQUISITE constraint stated immediately after the list: 'It is critical that these settings be configured prior to use. For example, the Client Managed Verification option for the Task Processor field must be selected, or the admin will not see either the Verification or Document Separation options.' Tool is available to the Invoice Configuration administrator (Unrestricted) role when Capture Processing (client-managed) is activated.

configFields.name: searchable
configFields.label: Searchable
configFields.sourceQuote: This is represented as a _Yes_ or _No_ variable under the Searchable column on the Vendor Form page.
configFields.notes: Two-value Yes/No attribute set under the Searchable column on the Vendor Form page (the corpus places it there; it does NOT state that the Vendor Form page and the Vendor Search Admin page are the same grid, so no such equivalence is asserted here). The attribute determines which fields the Vendor Search Admin tool can expose to quick search and advanced search. Documented constraint, stated verbatim in the same paragraph: "Note that while all fields can be added as columns in the vendor row grid, only selected fields can be used for the quick search and advanced search functionalities." So the Searchable value partitions the field set: every added field appears as a vendor-row-grid column regardless, but only Searchable=Yes fields reach quick/advanced search. fieldType mapped to the schema's boolean/two-value type ('checkbox') because the schema has no 'yes_no' member; the corpus calls it a "variable" and never documents the input widget, so no widget shape is claimed. Verified: grep -c '<table' on this file returns 0.

Binding, stated in the same file: the Invoice Admin accesses the Vendor Search Admin tool by clicking Administration > Invoice > Vendor Search Admin (left menu) — the corpus renders that path with non-breaking-space separators, so it is paraphrased here rather than quoted. Documented constraint from the same paragraph as the sourceQuote: "Note that while all fields can be added as columns in the vendor row grid, only selected fields can be used for the quick search and advanced search functionalities." — i.e. adding a field always yields a vendor-row-grid column, but quick/advanced search availability is governed separately by the Searchable Yes/No attribute. Illustration only (NOT an enumeration, per LOCKED RULE 6): "For example, the administrator can decide to add the _Tax Type_ or _Country_ fields as searchable items. These will appear as columns in the vendor row grid, but only the _Tax Type_ field will be available in quick search and advanced search." No field-picker catalog for this page exists anywhere in this corpus, so validValues is deliberately empty. fieldType left 'unknown' because the corpus never documents the add/remove widget shape and the repair instruction did not call the type wrong. Verified: grep -c '<table' on this file returns 0.

configFields.name: condition_left_parenthesis
