sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Done terminates the Copy > Rename > Done wizard and is distinct from the rule-set Save in order 19; the corpus then hands the sequence explicitly to the rule-authoring steps, which is why this step continues rather than ending here. SOURCE: "Continue to Step 2, Step 3, and Step 4 to add additional matching rules to the new PO matching rule." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-create-the-purchase-order-matching-rule-set-4d3866f3.md

sequence.action: reselect the newly named rule set and click Edit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The create wizard closes on Done and leaves you on the list page, so the set must be re-opened before any rule can be authored. Edit is also the control the In Use gate removes, which is why order 1 comes first. SOURCE: "On the Purchase Order Matching Rules page, select the rule set, and then click Edit." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md

sequence.action: select the Default named rules group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Default is a VALUE in this list, not a control, and the corpus states outright that it is the basis of the group you are about to author - pick the wrong group here and the rules in orders 9-18 attach to something the policy will never reach. SOURCE: "Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md

sequence.action: click to open the Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This is the window that actually contains the Life to Date and Rules tabs; without it the tabs are not reachable from the rule set. SOURCE: "Double-click the rule you want to use, and then, in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md CONTRADICTION - TAB DEPTH, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: step-3 skips Edit Rules entirely and places the tab one level up ("In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md). A driver must probe for the tabs at BOTH depths rather than fail on the first miss.

sequence.action: type a descriptive name for the new rule/rules group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Named before any rule type is selected, per the corpus order. The name is the identity the condition-based work in step grp3-condition-based-rule-group later selects against, so an unnamed group cannot be extended. SOURCE: "In Purchase Order Matching Rules, type a descriptive name for the new rule in Name." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md AMBIGUITY RECORDED: the sentence says 'a descriptive name for the new rule' while the surrounding topic is creating a named rules GROUP; the corpus does not settle which object is named. Do not assume.

sequence.action: click the Life to Date tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Life to Date is authored before the Rules tab because the corpus runs its own steps in that order and hands off explicitly at the end. SOURCE: "Proceed to Step 3 to add PO to Request fields matching rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.mdINFERRED:  beyond the hand-off: Life to Date rules compare against the CUMULATIVE sums of all invoices carrying the PO number, while Rules-type rules compare one invoice to one PO - so settling the cumulative envelope first gives the per-invoice rules a ceiling to sit inside. That reading is inferred from the two rule types' own descriptions, not stated as an ordering requirement.

sequence.action: select the check box next to each Life to Date rule type to activate
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The check box is what makes the tolerance controls exist at all - they are revealed per selection, so a driver that goes looking for a tolerance field before ticking a box will not find one. SOURCE: "As you select each check box, options appear that let you refine the tolerance." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md The six selectable rule types are enumerated in the canonical Life to Date table ("Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md).

sequence.action: set the tolerance basis for the selected Life to Date rule (Value, or Percentage)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Set immediately after each check box, while its revealed options are on screen; deferring it leaves a rule armed with no stated tolerance. SOURCE: "In the Overage Tolerance section, select Value or Percentage." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: configure-three-way-matching names this section "Overage Tolerance" with exactly TWO options, while step-2 leaves the section unnamed and offers a THIRD - Value bound to Currency with "- AND -", or Percentage. Probe for both shapes; the corpus does not say which provisioning shows which.

sequence.action: if the Value branch is taken, choose the company base currency
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Only meaningful on the Value branch, and only in the step-2 reading of the tolerance section - which is why it sits after order 12 rather than beside it. Skip it on a Value tolerance and cross-currency invoices are compared against an unstated base. SOURCE: "Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system. This functions as for other rule sets, including audit rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md OFF-PAGE, DO NOT LOOK FOR A TOGGLE HERE: the exchange rates this relies on are on by default and administered outside Invoice — "Exchange rates that allow currency conversion are on by default. As reference, this feature is accessed using the Expense Admin module." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/activate-exchange-rates-for-matching-rule-sets-c51af31c.md

sequence.action: (optional) click Change to open the exception message editor
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Change is the only documented door into the message editor; New and Save in orders 15 and 19 are controls INSIDE it, not on the rule window, so clicking them first is a category error. SOURCE: "Exception Message: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md

sequence.action: (optional) click New inside the editor and author the exception text
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Authored while the editor is open and committed with the editor's own Save before returning to the rule window. Scope warning that a driver will otherwise get wrong: this New creates a MESSAGE, never a rule set - rule-set creation is Copy > Rename > Done at orders 3-5. SOURCE: "Exception Message: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md

sequence.action: (optional) select the check box to let the invoice move despite the exception
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Decided on the same pass as the message, because together they define what the triggered rule DOES; leave it clear and every trip of this rule becomes a hard stop rather than a flag, which is a policy decision, not a default to assume. SOURCE: "Allow Submit/Approve: Select this check box to allow submission and processing of the invoice even if an exception is triggered." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md The corpus documents ONLY the selected state; do not infer the cleared state's label or a paired Yes/No value.

sequence.action: click the Rules tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The hand-off from the Life to Date work is explicit, which is what makes this ordering corpus-stated rather than a guess. SOURCE: "Proceed to Step 3 to add PO to Request fields matching rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md

sequence.action: select each unwanted default rule row and click Delete
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Do this BEFORE adding your own rules, not after. The set was born as a copy in order 3, so it arrives carrying the source set's rules; the corpus issues this as an instruction, not a suggestion, and skipping it is the classic silent half-work - your new rules fire correctly and the inherited ones fire too. SOURCE: "Be sure to clear the default rule set if you do not intend to use them." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md

sequence.action: select the rule level
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Level FIRST, because it repopulates the two field pickers below it - set Payment Request or Purchase Order before Level and the selection is discarded when Level changes. SOURCE: "As different levels are chosen in Level, different field sets will populate the selections available in Payment Request and Purchase Order." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: the enumerating step gives FOUR values ("Select a value from Level (Header, Vendor, Line Item, Line Item - Receipt), so the matching rule operates for the field(s) you want compared." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md) while that same file's intro paragraph gives THREE in a different order and omits the receipt level ("Rules-type matching rule sets are based on levels of Vendor, Header, and Line Item, and are applied by the system on a one-to-one basis between the current, incoming invoice and the PO." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md). The receipt level is also spelled with an ASCII hyphen here and an en dash in configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md - match on the visible words, not the dash.

sequence.action: select the invoice-side field
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Selected before the PO-side field, because the corpus states the PO list is filtered BY this choice - reverse the two and the PO selection is invalidated. SOURCE: "In the Payment Request list, select the request field to match to the same field in the PO." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md

sequence.action: select the PO-side field to compare against
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Strictly after order 20; the corpus says so in the step itself. The option catalogue is never published for the general case, so a driver must be handed the pair to select rather than enumerate it. SOURCE: "Under Purchase Order, select the PO field to match to the invoice (they will change depending on the field selected in the step above)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md

sequence.action: choose the tolerance for this rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Marked conditional on the field pair chosen above, so it can only be evaluated after orders 20-21 - a driver that expects an unconditional tolerance control will stall on rules that do not offer one. SOURCE: "(Optional depending on field choice) Determine what tolerance you will allow when the rule is triggered using options under Tolerance." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: step-3 enumerates FOUR options (None, Within (+/-), Custom, Currency) while configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md gives THREE and then a second choice — "If applicable, in the Tolerance section, select None, Within, or Custom, and then select Value or Percentage."

sequence.action: where the second tolerance choice is offered, set the basis
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Only exists in the three-way-matching reading of the Tolerance section, and only after a None/Within/Custom choice is made - which is why it is a separate order rather than folded into 22. SOURCE: "If applicable, in the Tolerance section, select None, Within, or Custom, and then select Value or Percentage." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md Distinct from the Value/Percentage pair in the Overage Tolerance section on the Life to Date tab (order 12); same words, different section, different rule type.

sequence.action: click Add to commit this rule into the rows
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Nothing entered in orders 19-23 exists as a rule until Add fires; a writer that moves straight to Save loses the in-progress rule silently, because Save commits the rows, not the editor. SOURCE: "Click Add to insert this rule into the rows under Rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md

sequence.action: read back the committed rule rows, then repeat orders 19-24 for each further rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The rows are the only documented confirmation that Add actually landed, which makes this the verification point of the whole authoring loop. SOURCE: "Then, as each rule is added using the Add button, they will appear at the bottom of the Rules window in rows." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md

sequence.action: click Save to commit the rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Terminal commit of the authoring session; the corpus ends the Rules-type procedure on it. SOURCE: "Click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md

sequence.action: select the PO policy that should use this rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Page switch, and this is the leg that turns a built rule set into a live one - the rule set is bound from Policies, never from the rule set page itself. configSteps.name: Configure three-way matching (invoice to PO to receipt) with receipt confirmation
configSteps.goal: Invoice lines are validated against both the purchase order and the goods receipts, with a Rules-tab Line Item - Receipt rule, a Life to Date Match against Received Quantity rule, a tolerance, an exception message, and a receipt confirmation type that tells the invoice owner what to do. SILENT HALF-WORKS: (a) build the rules before the Quantity Receipt file is imported and every line looks unreceived; (b) build only one of the two rules and the vendor recommendation of using all three is not met - the quantity envelope or the per-line check is missing with no error; (c) add the Delivery Slip Number field AFTER the rules are live and matching silently changes from sequential-by-receipt to DSN-targeted, with no fallback when no GRN carries the number; (d) configure any confirmation type without Is Receipt Required = Yes on the PO line and none of it is ever evaluated.

sequence.action: select the Payment Request Header form type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: FIRST, and this is the ordering fact that costs the most if missed: whether the Delivery Slip Number field exists on the header form decides what a Line Item - Receipt rule actually associates against. Add it later and the association logic changes underneath rules that are already live. SOURCE: "In the Form Type list, select the Payment Request Header form." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md CORPUS-STATED consequence of skipping it entirely: "If the admin does not add the Delivery Slip Number field to the form, Concur Invoice will perform the matching sequentially by receipt." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delivery-slip-number-field-for-three-way-matching-b0d3f1ca.md

sequence.action: select the specific header form to modify, then open Add Fields
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: The form list only populates after a form type is chosen, so this cannot precede order 1; inferred from the already-built Forms and Fields page record for formsTabList, whose own evidence states the list appears once a form type is selected. No new claim is made here.

sequence.action: select the Delivery Slip Number field in the Add Fields to Forms window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This is the optional leg the three-way matching topic names, and it is a decision with teeth rather than a cosmetic addition. SOURCE: "the admin should add the Delivery Slip Number field to the Payment Request Header form in the Forms and Fields tool." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md HARD NEGATIVE a driver cannot infer, CORPUS-STATED: once DSN is in play there is NO fallback — "If Concur Invoice does not find a GRN with the same DSN, it will not revert to the sequential association logic but will instead leave the invoice unassociated to the GRNs." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/receipt-association-and-three-way-matching-12b976a5.md

sequence.action: click Add Fields to commit the field onto the form
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Commits order 3; until this fires the field is selected but not on the form, and the matching behaviour is still the sequential one. SOURCE: "Click the Delivery Slip Number field, and then click Add Fields." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md

The import itself is a file interface, not an admin page in this graph.

sequence.action: select the rule group inside the opened rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The rules window belongs to a rule GROUP, not to the rule set, so the group must be chosen before the tabs exist. SOURCE: "Double-click the rule you want to use, and then, in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md

sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Opens the named window that holds both tabs used below. SOURCE: "in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules. The Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md

Match on words, not punctuation.

sequence.action: set the tolerance, then its basis
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Conditional on the field pair above, so it can only be set after orders 10-11. sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Follows the None/Within/Custom choice in the same sentence; leaving it unset leaves the tolerance with no stated units. sequence.action: click the Life to Date tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Second half of the three-way configuration; the corpus explicitly recommends running BOTH the Rules-tab receipt rule and the Life to Date received-quantity rule. sequence.action: select the received-quantity rule type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The cumulative counterpart of the per-line rule: it compares total invoiced quantities against total received quantities across every invoice sharing the PO number, which the per-line rule cannot see. SOURCE: "Click the Life to Date tab, and then select the Match against Received Quantity option." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md LABEL DRIFT, RECORDED: the same file writes "Matched against Received Quantity" in its overview bullet and "Match against Received Quantity" in its procedure and in the canonical table.

sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Appears only after the check box in order 19 is selected, and governs how far above the received quantity an invoice may go before the exception fires. sequence.action: click Save to commit both legs
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Terminal commit of the three-way configuration; the corpus ends the procedure here, after both tabs are done, not between them. SOURCE: "SAP Concur recommends that clients include all other rules that they typically use in any matching situation, such as unit price and vendor." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md CARDINALITY CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: this file names two rules and then recommends "all three" ("SAP Concur recommends that clients use all three of these rules for three-way matching."), while the tools-guides twin says three rules are available and recommends using "both" of them.

configSteps.name: Add a condition-based rule group to an existing named rules group (Multiple Matching Rule Sets)
configSteps.goal: One matching rule set carries several named rules groups, with a condition-based group nested under an existing group so that a different set of tolerances fires for a specific vendor, division, project or spend type. SILENT HALF-WORKS: (a) configure the conditions but never open Edit Rules on the new condition and you have a condition that detects something and then does nothing; (b) click Save in the conditions dialog but never Update after each rule and the rules do not land in the row; (c) attach the confirmation type to the wrong object - it can be set on the rule SET or on a rule CONDITION, and the two behave differently.

sequence.action: check the In Use status of the target rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same gate as every other edit on this page, and it bites hardest here because condition-based groups are usually added to a set that has already been in service. In Use = Yes means this whole procedure is impossible on that row; you must copy it first. SOURCE: "A rule set with an In Use status of Yes cannot be modified in any way." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

sequence.action: select the matching rule set and click Edit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The corpus opens this procedure exactly here; the condition-based group is added inside an existing set, never created standalone. SOURCE: "Select the matching rule set in Purchase Order Matching Rules and then click Edit." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: click Edit to open the rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Opens the set for editing; without it the rule groups list below is not reachable. SOURCE: "Select the matching rule set in Purchase Order Matching Rules and then click Edit." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: select the named rule group the condition-based group will sit under
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The parent group must be selected BEFORE Add, because the new group is created 'under' whatever is selected - Add with the wrong parent selected buries the conditions in the wrong branch of the set. SOURCE: "Select the named rule group within which the condition-based rule set will be included, then click Add." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.mdINFERRED:  Why this matters at all: the corpus describes the result as a set that can run across different PO types, with the conditions deciding which branch applies. Nesting under the wrong parent therefore mis-scopes the rules rather than erroring.

sequence.action: click Add to create the condition-based group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same label as the Rules-tab Add in the end-to-end step but a different act entirely: here it creates a nested group, there it commits a rule row. A driver must resolve Add by context, not by label. SOURCE: "Select the named rule group within which the condition-based rule set will be included, then click Add." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: configure the detection conditions in the group conditions dialog
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Conditions are authored before any rule, because they are what the rules will hang off; a rule authored first has no condition to be triggered by. SOURCE: "In Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions, configure the conditions that the system will detect and then execute the matching rule set on" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md This is a NESTED WINDOW of this page with no independent click path - do not treat it as a page.

sequence.action: click Insert for each additional condition, then Save the dialog
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Insert is per-condition and Save closes the dialog: Save without Insert loses the pending condition. SAP typo preserved in the source ('any addition conditions'). SOURCE: "Click Insert to add any addition conditions, and then click Save when you are done." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: select the new condition and click Edit Rules
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: THE STEP THAT IS EASIEST TO SKIP AND THE MOST DAMAGING TO SKIP: without it the condition is detected and nothing happens. Edit Rules on the NEW CONDITION - not on the parent group - is what specifies the consequence. SOURCE: "Select the new condition, and then click Edit Rules to specify what should happen when the system detects the condition" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: click Update after each rule to add it to the row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Update, not Add, is the commit inside the condition-based branch, and it is per-rule: author several rules and click Update once and only the last survives. sequence.action: click Save to commit the condition-based group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Terminal commit, explicitly after the last Update in the same sentence. SOURCE: "Add any additional rules, clicking Update after each new rule to add it to the row, then click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-add-condition-based-rule-to-a-named-rules-group-db93fb81.md

sequence.action: (optional) select the rule set or the rule condition and click Edit Confirmation
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Deliberately after the conditions exist: the corpus binds the confirmation text to the field type chosen when the rule group conditions were created, so doing this before order 6 has nothing to bind to. sequence.action: (optional) choose the confirmation type for this rule group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Chosen per rule group, which is why it belongs at the end of the condition work rather than at the top of it. configSteps.name: Change the matching rules on a rule set that has locked at In Use = Yes
configSteps.goal: A live PO policy ends up running amended matching rules even though the rule set it was running is permanently locked. SILENT HALF-WORKS AND HARD FAILURES: (a) trying to edit the locked set directly - it cannot be edited OR deleted, ever; (b) editing the copy and stopping there, leaving the policy still bound to the old locked set, so nothing changes in production while the admin believes it has; (c) taking the unlock route on a large invoice population - the corpus only calls it feasible when the number of associated invoices is small.

sequence.action: read the In Use column for the rule set that needs changing
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The whole branch turns on this one value. Yes is not a warning, it is a permanent lock on that object. SOURCE: "once a match rule set is run against a PO associated invoice a status of In Use is assigned and the rule set is locked: it cannot be edited or deleted from the system." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md ALTERNATIVE ROUTE, DELIBERATELY NOT EMITTED AS A SEQUENCE ENTRY BECAUSE ITS CONTROL IS NOT ON AN ADMIN PAGE: "A matching rule set with a status of In Use can be unlocked by breaking its association with all invoices it is associated with." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md; the control lives in the Actions menu of the end-user invoice list ("In the Actions menu, click Change to Non-PO." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/change-a-po-based-invoice-policy-to-a-non-po-based-invoice-policy-12786d77.md), and its LABEL IS CONTRADICTED across three topics - "Change to Non-PO", "Change to Non PO Invoice", and the imperative form above. After it succeeds: "Now, the rule set has a status of No and can be edited using the Edit button:"

sequence.action: select the locked rule set row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The locked set is the base to copy from, so it is selected rather than opened - a driver that tries Edit here gets nothing and may misread the lock as a broken control. SOURCE: "The administrator is restricted to editing only those PO matching rules that do not have a status of In Use." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md

sequence.action: click Copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Copy is the prescribed escape from the lock, and it is first because the whole remedy is a copy-edit-swap, in that order. SOURCE: "use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed, then change the PO Matching Ruleset value in Policies to implement the new rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

sequence.action: rename the copy, incrementing the version, and press Enter
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Naming discipline is load-bearing here rather than cosmetic: because every tested set locks, a tenant accumulates versions, and the corpus prescribes an incrementing convention so the production set can be identified later. SOURCE: "Repeat steps 1–3 for any additional changes, incrementing the version name each time." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md

sequence.action: click Done to close the copy wizard
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Closes the Copy > Rename > Done wizard before the copy can be opened for editing; it is not the rule-set Save. SOURCE: "3.  Click Done." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-create-the-purchase-order-matching-rule-set-4d3866f3.md

sequence.action: select the copy and click Edit, then amend its Life to Date and Rules configuration
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Edit works on the copy precisely because the copy has never run against an invoice, so its In Use is still No. The amendment itself follows the same two sub-procedures as the end-to-end step. SOURCE: "Change the matching rules configuration by following the procedures under Step 2: Create the Life to Date Matching Rule Set and Step 3: Create the PO to Request Fields Matching Rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md

sequence.action: click Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Commits the amended copy before the policy is pointed at it - swap first and the policy briefly runs a half-edited set against live invoices, which would lock it in that state. SOURCE: "4.  Click Save." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md

sequence.action: open the policy currently bound to the locked rule set
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Which policy to open is read off the locked set's own Associated Policies column, so this order depends on order 1 having been read properly. SOURCE: "Associated Policies: Shows what Invoice PO policy has been configured to include this PO matching rule set." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

sequence.action: change the selection to the amended copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: THE STEP THAT ACTUALLY CHANGES PRODUCTION. Everything before it is preparation; skip it and the policy keeps running the locked original while the admin believes the fix shipped. SOURCE: "use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed, then change the PO Matching Ruleset value in Policies to implement the new rules." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md The corpus states the same remedy as an ordered test loop: "Make edits, and, when you are finished, apply the rule set to the relevant policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md

sequence.action: read Associated Policies back on both rows to confirm the swap
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The only documented read-back that the binding moved. It is a display of the Policies selection, never an editable field on this page. SOURCE: "You select a rule set using the PO Matching Ruleset option in Policies." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md

configSteps.name: Configure a group-aware purchase order: numbering, transmittal messaging, branding and printed fields
configSteps.goal: One invoice group's purchase orders are generated with the intended number sequence and transmitted to vendors with the right company identity, message, sender address, attachments and printed field set. SILENT HALF-WORKS: (a) configure without first selecting the Group and the settings land on the wrong configuration - and a group that never gets one silently falls back to the Global Group; (b) set the Next Sequence casually and you are stuck, because once the system is in use the number can only be moved further along, never back; (c) pick the printed fields without first setting the Policy list and you have chosen fields for the wrong policy.

sequence.action: select the invoice Group this configuration is for, before creating or editing anything
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: FIRST, and the corpus says so in the plainest possible terms. Every field below is scoped by this choice; set them with the wrong group selected and they land on another subsidiary's transmittals. SOURCE: "Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you select before creating the configuration." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-configuration-is-group-aware-b603f04b.md AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT, CORPUS-STATED: "Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group configuration by default." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-configuration-is-group-aware-b603f04b.md: a group you forget simply inherits, with no error to notice. LOCATION UNATTESTED - REAL GAP, NOT AN OMISSION: the corpus never states WHERE the Group is selected; no Group control is documented on the tool itself. A driver must probe, not assume a picker on this page. ROLE GATE, CORPUS-STATED: "The Purchase Order Configuration tool is available to the Invoice Configuration administrator for setting default information for purchase orders. To view this tool, click Administration > Invoice > Purchase Order Configuration." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/use-the-purchase-order-configuration-tool-51009c8c.md

sequence.action: enter the starting PO number in the PO Number Generation section
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Do this before the system is in use, because afterwards it is one-way: the number can only be reset to one further along the sequence. There is also a 9-character limit on the PO number. SOURCE: "What you enter in the Next Sequence field will be the starting number, which can be altered once the system is in use only by using a number "further along" the numbering sequence in use" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md PLAN THE TEST NUMBERS DELIBERATELY, CORPUS-STATED: "TIP: For testing, plan your sequential number assignment so that, once testing is completed, the starting number sequence for production is what you want." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md.INFERRED:  UNDETERMINED, DO NOT ASSUME: whether the 9-character limit applies to the sequence alone or to prefix + sequence + postfix combined is never stated in this corpus.

sequence.action: set the PO number prefix
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Set alongside the sequence rather than later, because prefix, sequence and postfix compose one generated number and the 9-character ceiling is stated for the number as a whole. SOURCE: "The prefix and postfix of the PO number do not distinguish between uppercase and lowercase." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md LABEL WARNING: the corpus only ever writes this control in lowercase inside a Note ('prefix'), never as an on-screen label - a driver must probe for it rather than match a literal string.

sequence.action: set the PO number postfix
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same composition reason as order 3, and case-insensitive for the same stated reason. The only content guidance is a convention, not a rule, and no maximum length is documented for the postfix itself. SOURCE: "Typically, the Postfix value is the initials of the purchasing agents." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: enter the instructions that ride on the transmitted PO itself
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This message is printed on the purchase order, not in the carrying email - conflating it with the two email fields below is the classic mistake, and produces vendor instructions that never reach the document. SOURCE: "Enter instructions you want the vendor to note and follow." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md HARD LIMIT, CORPUS-STATED: "This field is limited to 3200 characters." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md. Do not carry this limit to the email fields.

sequence.action: set the default subject line for PO transmission emails
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Governs the carrying email, not the document - the counterpart to order 5. SOURCE: "The text entered in the Default Email Subject When Transmitting Purchase Orders field will appear in the subject field of the email sent to the vendor (the admin can customize this field)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md HARD LIMIT, CORPUS-STATED: "This field is limited to 500 characters." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md. UNENUMERATED: the corpus says a tool tip offers tokens for this field but NEVER lists them; do not import a token catalogue from any other topic.

sequence.action: set the default body text for PO transmission emails
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This one is a DEFAULT, not a lock - the corpus states it can be changed at review time before transmittal, so a writer should not treat a per-PO deviation as a configuration failure. No character limit is documented for this field; do not carry over the 3200 or 500 figures. SOURCE: "The text entered in the Default Email Message When Transmitting Purchase Orders field will appear in the body of the email sent to the vendor (note that this can be changed as you review the PO prior to transmittal):" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: enter the company address that prints on the PO
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Part of the group-varying company identity, so it belongs after the Group is settled in order 1. SOURCE: "Enter your company address in the Company Address field." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md FENCE: this is a single free-text address printed on the PO PDF. It is NOT the structured Ship To / Bill To address-book records on the already-built Company Locations page. Do not merge or re-home.

sequence.action: click Upload in the Company Branding Logo section
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Group-scoped and singular, which is exactly why order 1 has to be right first - there is one logo per invoice group and uploading under the wrong group overwrites that group's brand. SOURCE: "The logo is group-aware in the same way as the purchase order configuration and clients can only update one company logo per invoice group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md CONSTRAINTS, CORPUS-STATED: "The image should be 55 pixels high and no more than 200 pixels in length and 100 KB in size." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md, which also enumerates the accepted formats and the View / Remove controls.

sequence.action: type the desired prefix for the sender address
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Only the prefix is editable; the suffix is fixed. Leaving it BLANK is not a neutral default - it changes the From address to the requestor's own, which SAP explicitly does not recommend because of spam filtering. SOURCE: "If the prefix is left blank, the system will use the requestor’s email address as the "From" address." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md SCOPE CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: the same prefix lever is also given to the PO Processor at transmit time — "The processor can change the prefix for the From address but cannot change the suffix of the address" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md. So the configured value can be overridden downstream by a different role.

sequence.action: upload the documents that should ride along with every PO transmittal for this group
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Group-scoped like the logo, so again strictly after order 1. These are additive, not exclusive - they do not replace what the user attaches. SOURCE: "These documents apply to all PO transmissions performed by the PO Processor for that Group and are included alongside any documents added by the user." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/manage-images-03021850.md CORPUS-STATED effect: "These documents will be included when the supplier receives the PO." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: select the correct policy in the Policy list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: BEFORE the field selection below, and the corpus makes this an explicit instruction rather than an inference. Choose the printed fields with the wrong policy selected and you have configured a different policy's purchase orders. SOURCE: "The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order. Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md SAP TYPO PRESERVED: the source writes 'line time fields' for 'line item fields'. UNENUMERATED: the corpus never lists which policies appear here. Policy definition itself lives on the already-built Policies page; this is only the selector that scopes the field roster.

sequence.action: select the header and line item fields to print on the purchase order
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Strictly after order 12, per the same sentence. UNENUMERATED, AND THE GAP IS THE FINDING: the selectable header and line-item field roster is never listed anywhere in this corpus, so a driver must read the live list rather than expect a known set. SOURCE: "The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order. Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: (optional) select the header field that suppresses the requestor's name from the ship-to address
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Grouped after order 13 because the corpus describes it as a header field, i.e. a member of the same (unenumerated) printed-field roster, given its own explanatory paragraph. The ordering is inferred from that membership, not stated. CORPUS-STATED effect: "Instead, they can use the Ship To without Requestor Name header field, whereby the requestor’s name is omitted." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md LABEL DRIFT, RECORDED: the section heading capitalises 'Without' and the body sentence lowercases it, in the same file. Probe both.

sequence.action: (optional) select the header field that removes the company address from the transmitted PO
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Same membership and same reasoning as order 14 - a header field within the printed-field roster, so it follows order 13. CORPUS-STATED purpose, for cross-country PO creation: "Admins can select the Company Name without address header field for users who create purchase orders across countries and want to remove the purchase requester’s company address that is displayed on the transmitted purchase order." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md NOTE the interaction a writer should think about before setting it: order 8 fills a company address in precisely so it can print. This field suppresses it.

configSteps.name: Make purchase orders carry an email bill-to address instead of a physical one
configSteps.goal: Vendors receiving a transmitted PO see an email bill-to address that tells them where to send the invoice, instead of the physical address. THE FAILURE MODE IS ENTIRELY SILENT: if any of the three legs is missing the purchase order simply keeps printing the physical address exactly as before, with no error, no warning and nothing on the configuration page to indicate the feature is inert.

sequence.action: select the Purchase Order Header form type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: The whole ordering of this step is corpus-stated in one sentence, which makes both form work and address work PRECONDITIONS of the configuration selection, not companions to it: the admin can select the header field only 'provided' both are already done. SOURCE: "Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool and entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md Note the form is the PURCHASE ORDER Header form here, not the Payment Request Header form used by the Delivery Slip Number leg of three-way matching.

sequence.action: select the specific PO header form and open Add Fields
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: The form list only populates after a form type is chosen, so this cannot precede order 1; inferred from the already-built Forms and Fields page record, not from any new claim in this run.

sequence.action: select the Use Email as Bill-To field
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Leg one of the stated precondition. Without the field on the form there is nothing for the configuration selection in order 8 to expose. SOURCE: "Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool and entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: click Add Fields to commit the field onto the form
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Commit for order 3; the field is not on the form until the confirm control fires. Inferred from the already-built Forms and Fields add-fields procedure, whose confirm control is this field.

sequence.action: open the Bill To tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Leg two, and it must be the Bill To side specifically - a ship-to record carries no bill-to email for the PO to use. SOURCE: "Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool and entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: create or open the bill-to location record
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: A location record must exist before an email address can be stored on it; inferred from the already-built Company Locations page structure, where the address record is the container for the email field in order 7.

sequence.action: enter the bill-to email address
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: This is the value the vendor will actually be told to send the invoice to, so an empty one is exactly the silent-failure case in this step's goal. SOURCE: "The bill-to address on the PO PDF that the vendor receives is an email address which notifies the vendor to send the PO to the specified email address." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md CORPUS-STATED variant for capture clients: "Clients who use the capture service can use their capture email address as the bill-to address." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md.

sequence.action: click Save to store the address
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: Commit for orders 6-7 on the already-built Company Locations page; an unsaved address is not visible to the purchase order at transmit time.

sequence.action: select the correct policy in the Policy list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: Same gate as in the group-aware configuration step: the header field roster is scoped by the selected policy, so selecting the bill-to header field before setting this configures the wrong policy's purchase orders. SOURCE: "The header and line time fields you select will appear on the purchase order. Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

sequence.action: select the bill-to header field within the printed field roster
sequence.rationale: INFERRED: The control being set in order 11 is described by the corpus as a 'header field', i.e. a member of this (unenumerated) roster, so it is reached through this control. That containment is inferred from the wording 'header field'; the corpus never enumerates the roster, so a driver must read the live list.

sequence.action: select Use Email as Bill-To
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: LAST, because the sentence that documents it makes it conditional on orders 1-8 having already happened. And the consequence of getting the order wrong is invisible rather than loud. SOURCE: "If clients have not configured this feature, the purchase order will use the physical address as it does today." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md

configSteps.name: Stand up a new invoice approval workflow end to end (Approval Statuses -> Copy -> General -> Steps -> Step Rules -> Policy)
configSteps.goal: A brand-new invoice approval workflow exists, is fully stepped and ruled, and is actually in force because a policy points at it. Half-works if a leg is skipped: (a) skip the Approval Statuses tab and the Initial Status list on every step offers only the shipped defaults, so the custom status you meant to drive skip-to-step behaviour with silently does not exist; (b) skip the Copy and there is nothing to configure at all - the corpus states the administrator cannot create a workflow from scratch; (c) build steps but never attach the workflow to a policy and the whole object is inert - nothing routes through it, and worse, once it IS attached it can no longer be deleted; (d) author step rules before the steps exist and the Step Rules page has nothing to attach them to.

sequence.action: on the Approval Statuses tab > Invoice sub-tab, click New and type the name of each custom approval status the workflow will use
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is literally step 1 of SAP's own ordered list: 'When creating custom invoice workflows, an administrator should perform these steps in the following order:' followed by 'Create any custom approval statuses that you may use in the workflow.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md). Run out of order and the Initial Status list on the Add Workflow Step page has no custom entry to offer - work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md states 'You can also create custom approval statuses.' as the source of that list.

sequence.action: type the action text that will become the approver's button label for this status
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type descriptive text to be used as the action text. This text becomes button text for the approver.' (adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md). This is the only place the on-screen button label is set; leaving it until after the workflow is built means approvers see an unlabelled or default action for whatever period elapses.

sequence.action: type the description text for the status
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type the description text.' (adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md). Ordering is internal to the Request Status window - it must be filled before Save on the same window, not after.

sequence.action: select the group configuration(s) permitted to edit this status, then Save the Request Status window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the group configuration(s) that can edit this workflow.' (adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md). INFERRED consequence of running it late: this is a rights field, so a status saved with the wrong group is editable by the wrong administrators from the moment it is saved.

sequence.action: on the Workflows tab select the workflow that most closely matches the target and click Copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and non-negotiable: 'To create a new workflow, an administrator must copy an existing invoice workflow and make the appropriate edits.' and 'The administrator cannot create a workflow from scratch.' (create-a-new-workflow-15992497.md). There is no 'New' entry point on the Workflows tab; an automation driver that looks for one stalls. The documented order agrees: 'Create a workflow by copying an existing workflow or the default workflow.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md).

sequence.action: on the General page (wizard page 1 of 3) read back Workflow Type and confirm it is the flavour you intended
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This field is read-only. It identifies the type of workflow that you chose to edit.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). Because it is read-only and inherited from the copy source, order 5 is the ONLY moment the type can be chosen. Discovering the wrong type after the steps are built means discarding the object and copying again.

sequence.action: type a new name for the workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type a new name for the workflow. This name does not have to be unique.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). Because names need not be unique, an unrenamed copy is indistinguishable from its source in the Workflows tab list and in the Policies page's workflow list - a driver that assigns by name can bind the policy to the wrong object. Rename before anything selects the workflow by name.

sequence.action: select the group rights an administrator must hold to modify this workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the group rights that an administrator must have in order to modify this workflow.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). CONTRADICTION WORTH DRIVING CAREFULLY: invoice-settings-cace748d.md states that if the Settings-tab own-approver check box is cleared, 'If this check box is not selected, then it overrides the Editable By Group(s) and Steps Can Be Added By fields on the Edit Workflow page and the Add/Edit Workflow Steps page.' - so a value set here can be silently overridden by a control on a different tab, and setting the Settings tab afterwards raises a conflict error.

sequence.action: choose who may add ad hoc steps to this workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED gate on two later General-page fields: 'This field is available only if you have chosen an option in the Steps Can Be Added field.' gates the employee-added-step email option, and 'This field is only available if you have chosen an option in the Steps Can Be Added field field.' (SAP's own duplicated word) gates Restrict Authorized Approver for - both in create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md. Leave this empty and those two controls are not merely default, they are absent from the page.

sequence.action: select the action to take when an approver has not approved within the allowed time
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This setting only appears if the admin has selected an option in the Approval Time Expired field.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md) - the day-count field below does not render until this list has a value. The same file gives the OR-gate for the extension field: 'This option is only available if either the Approval Time Expired Action or Assignment Timeout Action options are enabled.'

sequence.action: type the number of days after which the approval expires
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional visibility, the reverse side of order 10: 'This setting only appears if the admin has selected an option in the Approval Time Expired field.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). A driver that tries this field first finds nothing and, if it silently continues, ships a timeout action with no timeout.

sequence.action: click Next to leave the General page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED wizard transition: 'Click Next.' followed by 'The Steps page appears.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). The Steps page is a wizard page reached only through this button on a workflow already copied - it is not a separate left-menu destination, so there is no way to reach it before orders 5-11 are done.

sequence.action: on the Steps page click New to open the Add Workflow Step window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'On the Steps page, click New.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). INFERRED from the wizard structure documented in create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md: the Steps page only exists inside the workflow object opened at order 5, so every step created here belongs to that copy and cannot be authored in advance.

sequence.action: type the step name the employee will see on the Approval Flow page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type any alphanumeric name for the workflow step.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md), which also warns the name appears to the employee. INFERRED: naming is first in the window because the remaining fields (Role, Approval Actions) change which controls render, and renaming afterwards means re-opening a saved step.

sequence.action: select the role responsible for completing this step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the single most order-sensitive control on the Steps page. work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md: 'such as Authorized Approver, Invoice Approver, Invoice Processor, Invoice Processor Manager, or Invoice Vendor Manager' - and if it is a non-system role 'you must select an action or multiple actions in the Approval Actions field.' The same file: 'If you select Authorized Approver, two check boxes appear to select whether or not the authorized approver is based on limit or exception level of the invoice.' Set Role last and the fields you needed were never on screen.

sequence.action: pick the approval actions this approver may take
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'From the Approval Actions helper pane, click an action that an approver can make to an invoice that is awaiting approval.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). The same file states this field is REQUIRED for any non-system role, and that the control switches between multi-select and single-select depending on the Role chosen at order 15 - so it must follow Role, never precede it.

sequence.action: select who may edit the approver on this step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED CROSS-TAB GATE: 'If you have the Allow users to select their own approver for payment request field on the Settings page not selected, then the employee does not appear as an option.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). The employee option is missing from this list entirely unless the Settings tab was set first - so if a centralized workflow is intended, set the Settings tab BEFORE this step, or the value you pick here is later overridden with a conflict error per invoice-settings-cace748d.md.

sequence.action: select who may delete this step from the Approval Flow page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select who can delete this step on the Approval Flow page within Invoice, the employee, approver, or both.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). INFERRED ordering: this is a per-step right, so it must be set while the step window is open; there is no documented bulk pass to apply it to steps already saved.

sequence.action: select the approval status the invoice takes when this step begins
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED dependency on order 1: 'Click an approval status that represents what the invoice status should be set to when the Step begins, such as Pending Approval.' and, in the same row, 'You can also create custom approval statuses.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). If the Approval Statuses tab was skipped, this list simply lacks the custom status and the step silently keeps a default - a workflow that looks configured and routes wrongly.

sequence.action: save the step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save to return to the Workflows page.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). INFERRED: the save is what makes the step addressable by the Step Rules page at order 22 - an unsaved step cannot carry a rule.

sequence.action: use the Step Order column to put the saved steps in the intended sequence
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'To place the steps in the proper workflow order, use the Step Order column.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). HARD ORDERING RULE that must be honoured here and not discovered later: 'The Vendor Approval system step _cannot_ precede the Cost Object Approval step.' (step-3-edit-the-workflow-steps-f2731590.md). ROLE GATE on this action, quoted: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Workflows section in Administration.' (same file).

sequence.action: on the Step Rules page select a step and click New, then name the rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the reason this leg is last: 'Once you have created the workflow steps, you can attach rules to each step.' (work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md). The same file also states 'Not all steps can have rules. If the selected step can have a rule, the New button becomes available.' - so a driver must select a step first and read the New button's state rather than assume every step accepts a rule.

sequence.action: decide whether this rule is always evaluated or only when the other rules on the step are false
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'If the check box is _not_ selected, then the rule is evaluated and executed only if all other rules in this step were determined to be false.' (work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md). INFERRED ordering consequence: because the default behaviour is order-dependent across rules on the same step, adding a second rule later can change whether the first one ever fires - set this deliberately on every rule, not just the first.

sequence.action: in the Edit Action window select the action the rule performs
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED CARDINALITY LIMIT that constrains what can be added afterwards: 'A single workflow rule can contain only one of these actions:' - Skip step, Change approver, Send back to employee (work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md), while Generate an exception and Send email may repeat. A driver that appends a second exclusive action to an existing rule is rejected; it must author a second rule instead.

sequence.action: confirm the condition in the Edit Condition window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click OK.' (edit-workflow-rules-and-actions-abdf9b11.md). INFERRED: the condition is the 'if' half of the rule described in work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md ('Create a condition (the "if" portion...)'), so it must be committed before the action window can be reached and before the rule is meaningful.

sequence.action: click Done to leave the workflow wizard
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Done.' (edit-workflow-properties-409a8f0b.md). INFERRED: Done is the exit from the three-page wizard; until it is clicked the workflow object is still in the editor and the Policies page has nothing new to select.

sequence.action: open the target policy and select the new workflow in the Invoice Workflow list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 8 of the documented order: 'Assign the invoice workflow to a policy.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md), reinforced by 'Once you have created the workflow, you must associate it to a policy.' (create-a-new-workflow-15992497.md). Skip this and the workflow exists but nothing routes through it. LABEL DRIFT TO EXPECT: activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md describes this same list as 'In the Expense Report Workflow list, choose the appropriate workflow.' - two different labels in the corpus for the same association.

sequence.action: save the policy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md, policy association procedure). ONE-WAY DOOR the operator should know before saving: 'The system does not allow you to delete a workflow that is currently assigned to a policy.' (delete-a-workflow-or-workflow-steps-e9a84a07.md) - after this save, removing the workflow requires unassigning it here first.

configSteps.name: Configure the Authorized Approver feature (hierarchy first, then activation, then steps, then the approver list)
configSteps.goal: Invoices route to approvers whose authority is bounded by an approval limit and/or an exception range, driven by a real hierarchy. The corpus makes the ordering a hard blocker rather than a preference: without the Feature Hierarchies leg the feature cannot even be activated; without activation the ad hoc restriction options are absent from the workflow; without a step whose Role is Authorized Approver the feature is inert; and without a level on that step the Level field never appears on the approver record, so every approver ends up unlevelled and the filtering silently does nothing.

sequence.action: create the list that will back the Authorized Approver hierarchy and give it a descriptive name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD BLOCKER: 'and import/create its associated source list before the authorized approver feature can be activated.' (understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md). The Global-group-vs-hierarchy matrix states the same requirement as step 1 of the hierarchy column: 'Create a connected (multi-level) list of the hierarchy levels.' (global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md). A driver that opens Workflows first finds the feature unactivatable.

sequence.action: add each list item's code
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the reason codes must be settled before anything downstream reads them: 'The code format (EAST; NORTH) for each list item must be typed exactly as you have entered them here in your import.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). Changing a code after the hierarchy and any import reference it breaks the match silently.

sequence.action: add each list item's display name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the source list items are what the hierarchy levels resolve to - 'The source list is the hierarchical structure that will become the named vendor groups to which vendors will be assigned.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md, describing the same list-building procedure). INFERRED: names are cosmetic where codes are load-bearing, so they may be edited later without breaking the match - unlike order 2.

sequence.action: add sub-levels if the hierarchy is to be multi-level, then click Done
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Create a connected (multi-level) list of the hierarchy levels.' (global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md) and, from the parallel vendor-access procedure, 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). Depth added after the hierarchy is mapped leaves hierarchy levels and list levels out of step.

sequence.action: click Done to close out the list
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the list-building procedure in step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md, which ends the item loop with 'Click Done when all list items have been added.' The list must be complete and closed before it can be picked as a Source List on Feature Hierarchies.

sequence.action: select the Invoice Authorized Approver feature hierarchy from the landing screen
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the hierarchy is defined here and nowhere else - 'You must define the authorized approver hierarchy (Invoice' ... 'Feature Hierarchies)' per understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md (quote continues 'and import/create its associated source list before the authorized approver feature can be activated.'). The workflow-creation order names the same leg: '(Optional) Set up the Payment Authorized Approvers hierarchy if you choose to use authorized approvers.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md) - optional only because authorized approvers themselves are optional, not because the ordering is.

sequence.action: click Modify Hierarchy to open the detail editor
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Modify Hierarchy.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). ROLE GATE, quoted: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Feature Hierarchies section in Administration.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) - a Workflows-only administrator cannot complete this leg at all.

sequence.action: select the list built in orders 1-5 as the Source List
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the resolution of the prerequisite: 'In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The corpus is explicit that the list must pre-exist: 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md).

sequence.action: click New to add a level row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED: level rows and segment rows are paired one-to-one, so a level must be created before a segment can be assigned to it.

sequence.action: set the level for the row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, AND THE CORPUS CONTRADICTS ITSELF HERE - recorded rather than reconciled: step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md says of the Vendor Employee Access hierarchy 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).', while professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md instructs 'Set the level to Request.' for the Invoice Payment hierarchy. The corpus gives different level behaviour per feature hierarchy; do not assume either is universal. CONSEQUENCE OF LEVEL COUNT, corpus-stated in the same family: whether the hierarchy carries at least one level beyond Global determines which control User Administration later exposes.

sequence.action: select the field that acts as the hierarchy path segment for this level
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Segment Name list, select the field that will act as the list in User Permissions' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The field must already exist and already be tied to the source list - 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md) - so a segment chosen before the field is configured resolves to nothing.

sequence.action: click Save to commit the hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). This save is the boundary the Workflows leg depends on: only after it does the activation gate in order 13 become satisfiable.

sequence.action: on the Authorized Approvers tab > Configuration sub-tab, select the feature activation check box
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'To activate the feature, select Authorized Approver feature is available for workflows.' (procedure-2d20b513.md), and this is step 2 of the two-column configuration matrix in global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md (required for BOTH the global-group-only path and the hierarchy path). It is also a visibility gate on a General-page control: the ad hoc restriction options 'do not appear in Workflow until you have selected Authorized Approver feature is available for workflows on the Configuration tab of the Authorized Approvers tab.' (understand-ad-hoc-steps-ce0af3e7.md).

sequence.action: enter the minimum exception level authorized approvers may approve
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Enter the minimum exception level that authorized approvers can approve.' (procedure-2d20b513.md), listed as step 2's second half in the matrix: 'For exception-based approval configurations, define the upper and lower exception level.' (global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md). SCOPE WARNING, corpus-stated: 'The range is set in Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Authorized Approver tab.' and it applies to ALL exception-based authorized approvers (configuration-8b3be88b.md) - it is not a per-approver value, so setting it after approvers exist retroactively changes every one of them.

sequence.action: enter the maximum exception level authorized approvers may approve, then Save the Configuration sub-tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Enter the maximum exception level that authorized approvers can approve.' (procedure-2d20b513.md). Same all-approver scope as order 14 per configuration-8b3be88b.md. INFERRED: leaving the range unset while giving individual approvers the exception right at order 25 ('Select the check box to give this authorized approver exception approval.' - authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md) produces approvers with exception rights but no band to exercise them in.

sequence.action: on the Workflows tab select the target workflow and click Modify, then open the Steps page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the desired workflow and click Modify.' (edit-workflow-properties-409a8f0b.md); the authorized-approver procedure enters the same way and then goes 'On the  Steps page, click New. The Add Workflow Step window appears.' (create-an-authorized-approver-step-4640b5a5.md). INFERRED: the workflow must already exist - this step presumes the workflow from grpworkflows-s1, or an existing one.

sequence.action: set the step's Role to Authorized Approver
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the reason activation alone is not enough: 'An authorized approver is only used if set up as a step(s) in a workflow process.' (authorized-approvers-8b3ab7ad.md). Setting Role is also what renders the next three controls: 'If you select Authorized Approver, two check boxes appear to select whether or not the authorized approver is based on limit or exception level of the invoice.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md).

sequence.action: select the limit-authority restriction if the step should only accept limit-approved approvers
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Restrict approvers to those with limit authority to limit the type of authorized approver.' (create-an-authorized-approver-step-4640b5a5.md). The same file states the fail-open consequence of skipping both check boxes: 'If neither of these is checked, any approver may be used for the step, but the limit-approved or exception-approved indicator will be set only if the approver is authorized.' - the step LOOKS restricted and is not.

sequence.action: select the exception-authority restriction if the step should only accept exception-approved approvers
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Restrict approvers to those with exception authority to limit the type of authorized approver.' (create-an-authorized-approver-step-4640b5a5.md). Depends on the exception range set at orders 14-15: configuration-8b3be88b.md states the min/max 'range applies to all exception-based authorized approvers', so this restriction is meaningless until that range exists.

sequence.action: enter the authorized approver level that this step requires
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED VISIBILITY GATE: 'The Authorized Approver Level field appears only if the Authorized Approver option is selected in the Role field.' (step-1-assign-the-level-to-the-workflow-step-6035f10a.md). This is also the hinge for order 23 - see that entry.

sequence.action: save the workflow step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the authorized-approver step procedure ends 'Click Save.' before moving to rules (create-an-authorized-approver-step-4640b5a5.md). INFERRED: the save is what publishes the level to the Authorized Approver List, which is why order 23 can only work afterwards.

sequence.action: on the Authorized Approvers tab > Authorized Approver List sub-tab, expand the hierarchy tree, select the group, click New and pick the approver
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED dependency back on the Feature Hierarchies leg: 'The groups that appear here are from the Authorized Approver Hierarchy.' (authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md). Run this before orders 6-12 and the left-hand tree has no groups to select, so 'Select the group that is associated this authorized approver.' (same file) cannot be performed.
