The documented workflow order also puts this after the hierarchy: '(Optional) Add authorized approvers, if you choose to use authorized approvers.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md).

sequence.action: enter the level number on the approver record so this approver matches the step's required level
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, the sharpest ordering trap in this procedure: 'Once the level is added to the workflow step (described above), the Level field will appear in the New Authorized Approver and Modify Authorized Approver window.' (step-2-assign-the-level-to-the-approver-d8bf669c.md), corroborated by 'The Level field appears if levels have been assigned to a workflow approval step.' (authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md). Do order 20 first or this field is simply not on screen and every approver is saved unlevelled - the step's level filter then matches nobody.

sequence.action: set the approver's approval limit currency and amount
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'If you want this authorized approver to have limit approval, select the currency and the amount.' (authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md). Per-approver by design: 'The amount is set for each approver in the Authorized Approver List, in User Administration, or in the employee import.' (configuration-8b3be88b.md) - unlike the exception range, which is global.

sequence.action: tick the exception-approval right for this approver
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the check box to give this authorized approver exception approval.' (authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md). Order matters against orders 14-15: without the global min/max range the exception-approval right exists with no band, and against order 19: the step restriction filters on this flag, so approvers ticked after the step goes live are invisible to it until then.

sequence.action: back on the workflow's General page, choose who may add ad hoc steps
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED prerequisite for order 27: 'This field is only available if you have chosen an option in the Steps Can Be Added field field.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md - SAP's duplicated word preserved). Without a value here the ad hoc restriction control does not render.

sequence.action: restrict ad hoc approval steps to authorized approvers
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED DOUBLE GATE - this control needs BOTH order 13 and order 26: 'do not appear in Workflow until you have selected Authorized Approver feature is available for workflows on the Configuration tab of the Authorized Approvers tab.' (understand-ad-hoc-steps-ce0af3e7.md), plus the Steps-Can-Be-Added gate quoted at order 26. Skip either and users keep inserting ad hoc steps to unauthorized approvers while the workflow appears configured.

sequence.action: assign authorized approver rights to users as an alternative or supplement to the Authorized Approver List
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED alternative path: step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md lists three routes and states 'Regardless of how the authorized approvers are entered into Invoice, they all appear in the Authorized Approver List.' - so this leg is interchangeable with orders 22-25, not additional to them. The destination IS a built page as of 2026-09-01: the Authorized Approval Limits window (group Approval Authority), reached through Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration. The earlier claim that it was out of scope and that no page node should be created was reversed that day.

configSteps.name: Build a Vendor Employee Access hierarchy across the six tools in SAP's stated order
configSteps.goal: Vendors are partitioned into named groups and each employee can be pointed at exactly one group, so an invoice user only sees their own vendors. This is the procedure the corpus most explicitly orders, and every leg is load-bearing: the list supplies the codes, the hierarchy binds a custom field to those codes, Group Configurations creates groups whose names must match the list levels, and Forms and Fields is what EXPOSES the custom field on the Employee form. Skip the Forms and Fields leg and the whole chain is invisible - the User Administrator has no field to pick the vendor group from, so the hierarchy exists and nothing uses it.

sequence.action: create the source list and name it
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 1 of an explicitly ordered six-tool sequence: 'The administrator uses the following tools in the order presented to configure the feature.' - List Management, Feature Hierarchies, Group Configurations, Forms and Fields, Vendor Employee Access Import, User Administration (overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md). ROLE GATE, quoted from the same sentence: 'All tasks require the Invoice Configuration administrator role unless' (noted otherwise).

sequence.action: add each list item's code, recording it exactly
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and the single most brittle value in this procedure: 'The code format (EAST; NORTH) for each list item must be typed exactly as you have entered them here in your import.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). The Vendor Employee Access import at tool 5 matches on these codes; changing one afterwards breaks the mapping with no error at configuration time.

sequence.action: add each list item's name - these become the named vendor groups
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'The source list is the hierarchical structure that will become the named vendor groups to which vendors will be assigned.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). Order 6 depends directly on these names: 'In this step you will create groups that match the source list levels you created in Step 1 and matched to the feature hierarchy in Step 2.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md).

sequence.action: add sub-levels now if multi-level vendor groups are intended
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). Depth decided here propagates into the hierarchy segments (order 9), the group tree (order 7) and the Connected Lists tab (order 14); adding it later means revisiting all four.

sequence.action: click Done to close the list
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the list procedure's own closing instruction, 'Click Done when all list items have been added.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). A list left open is not selectable as a Source List on the next page.

sequence.action: select the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy and click Modify Hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 2 of the six-tool order: 'On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.' and 'In this step you will associate the source list you created in Step 1' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The page is a sibling left-menu tool, not a sub-page of List Management: 'Click List Management (left menu).' appears in step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md and 'Click Feature Hierarchies (left menu).' in step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md.

sequence.action: click Modify Hierarchy to open the editor
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Modify Hierarchy.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). INFERRED: the Source List, Level and Segment Name controls live inside this editor, so nothing on this page can be configured from the landing screen alone.

sequence.action: pick the list created at order 1 in Source List
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). This is exactly why List Management is step 1 and not step 2 - the list must be selectable before the hierarchy can bind to it.

sequence.action: click New to add a level row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The row must exist before a segment can be attached to it.

sequence.action: accept Employee as the level for this hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and explicitly not a choice on this hierarchy: 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). CONTRADICTION ACROSS FEATURE HIERARCHIES, recorded not reconciled: professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md instructs 'Set the level to Request.' for the Invoice Payment hierarchy - so a driver must not carry either level value across hierarchies.

sequence.action: select the custom field that will act as the segment (the corpus example uses Custom 02)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the field named HERE is the one exposed at order 13: 'In this step you will add the field (Custom 02) specified in the Feature Hierarchies step (Step 2) to the Employee form.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). Choose a different field on the form than the one named here and the two ends of the chain never meet.

sequence.action: click Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED: the hierarchy must be committed before the group names created at order 13 can be checked against the list levels it maps.

sequence.action: open the Vendor Access tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 3 of the six-tool order: 'Click the Vendor Access tab.' within 'In this step you will create groups that match the source list levels you created in Step 1 and matched to the feature hierarchy in Step 2.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md). Both prior legs must be finished because this step is defined by matching them.

sequence.action: click New to open the Select Group window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the procedure at step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md runs 'Click New to open the Select Group window.' INFERRED: the Global tree it opens is only meaningful once the hierarchy from orders 6-12 exists.

sequence.action: open the Global list, select the group name at its level and click Done
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, including the multi-level case: 'Multi-level list: To select a sub-group, open the list further and select the group name at its level, then click Done.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md). The depth available here is the depth created at order 4 - which is why sub-levels cannot be deferred.

sequence.action: type the vendor group name and Save, repeating until the named groups match the source list items
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED naming constraint that only bites at this point in the order: 'In this instance, the name does not need to match any existing code and may be descriptive. It cannot be the name of any existing group name already in the system.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md). The same step requires 'repeating until the named groups match those you created for your source list in Step 1' - a mismatch here is the classic silent half-configuration.

sequence.action: set Form Type to Employee
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 4 of the six-tool order: 'In Form Type, select Employee.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). This is the leg whose omission makes the whole chain invisible - the same file states the purpose plainly: 'Doing this allows this field to be exposed in the User Administration' (Expense and Invoice Settings page).

sequence.action: select the form under Form Name on the Forms tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Forms tab, first select the form under Form Name, then click Add Fields.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). The corpus states the selection order explicitly in that one sentence - form first, Add Fields second - so a driver that clicks Add Fields with no form selected has nothing to add to.

sequence.action: click Add Fields
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, same sentence as order 18: 'first select the form under Form Name, then click Add Fields.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md).

sequence.action: select the custom field named at order 11 in the Add Fields to Forms selector
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In Add Fields to Forms, select a field (Custom 02 in example below) and click Add Fields, repeating the process if multiple levels are to be added.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). It must be the SAME field chosen as the hierarchy segment - the file ties the two steps together explicitly ('the field (Custom 02) specified in the Feature Hierarchies step (Step 2)').

sequence.action: confirm the addition
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the same instruction ends 'and click Add Fields, repeating the process if multiple levels are to be added.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). INFERRED: the repetition count is set by the level depth chosen at order 4 - one field per level.

sequence.action: optionally rename the field on the Form Fields tab so users see a meaningful label
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and explicitly optional, but the corpus flags that its example depends on it: 'In the example below, Custom 02 is renamed to _Choose Vendor Access Group_ and is used for examples in this document. You have the option of renaming the Custom field in Step 4.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED ordering: rename AFTER adding, since the rename acts on a field already on the form.

sequence.action: if the vendor groups are multi-level, configure the fields on the Connected Lists tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and conditional on order 4: 'Use the Connected Lists tab if you have created a multi-level vendor group list' and '(Optional): If creating a multi-level list, click the Connected Lists tab and configure your fields by first selecting the list, then following the steps.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). Skip it on a multi-level list and the second and third fields do not filter from the first.

sequence.action: select the named vendor group for the user using the newly added field
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as step 6 of the ordered tool list, but recorded as a FORWARD REFERENCE THAT STAYS UNRESOLVED: 'The User Administrator accesses User Administration and uses the newly-added field in Step 6 to select the named vendor group' (overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md). The same source flags this as the one tool NOT covered by the Invoice Configuration administrator role. The conclusion stands but the reason has changed: the vendor-group selector lives on the User Administration USER PROFILE, which is unbuilt because its documentation defers to an external Shared guide absent from this corpus - NOT because of its menu location. Administration > Company is no longer out of scope for this graph; the Authorized Approval Limits window under it was built 2026-09-01.

configSteps.name: Author a workflow email notification on its tab, then select it on the workflow's General page
configSteps.goal: Approvers and submitters receive a customised notification rather than the shipped default. Two things half-work if the order is broken: authoring a notification and never selecting it on a workflow means it is inert (the corpus is explicit that assignment happens on a different tab); and selecting a notification before authoring one means the General-page lists offer only the stock entries. A third, non-configurable dependency exists downstream: whatever is set here, delivery still depends on the recipient's own Profile setting.

sequence.action: on the Email Notifications tab, filter the list to Payment Requests Notifications or Purchase Request Notifications and select a notification to copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the reason a copy is the only entry point: 'Add a new email notification by copying an existing notification, then editing the copy.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md), reached via 'in the Find workflow emails where list, select Payment Requests Notifications or Purchase Request Notifications.' (same file). A driver looking for a 'New' button on this tab finds none.

sequence.action: on the General step of the Modify Email Notification window, set the notification name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD LIMIT ON THE FRESH COPY: 'The only fields that can be edited at this time are Email Notification Name and Display as From.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). Everything else on the General step is locked until the copy is saved and reopened - the same file says 'If you need to make changes to the other fields, save this copy and then edit it as detailed in Modifying an Email Notification in this guide.' This name is also what appears in the workflow's notification lists at orders 8-11 (modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md: 'This name will appear in the email notification list while editing the workflow.'), so an unrenamed copy is unpickable.

sequence.action: set the from-address recipients will see
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type the email address you would like the recipient to see when they receive the notification.' (modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md), and it is the second of only two fields editable on the fresh copy per add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md. Miss it in this window and it requires a second save-and-reopen pass.

sequence.action: click Next to move to the Primary Recipient step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED wizard transition within the Modify Email Notification window - the procedure at add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md runs General -> Primary Recipient -> Delegate Recipient via Next. INFERRED: the Subject and Body controls are per wizard step, so a driver must traverse the steps rather than expecting one flat form.

sequence.action: edit the Email Subject on the Primary Recipient step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Make the desired changes to the Email Subject field.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). SPLIT WARNING FOR AN AUTOMATION DRIVER: the same file documents this field TWICE, once on the Primary Recipient step and once on the Delegate Recipient step. Filling the primary subject does NOT fill the delegate subject; they are two controls sharing one label and must be addressed separately.

sequence.action: edit the Email Body on the Primary Recipient step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Make the desired changes to the Email Body field.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). Same two-instance caveat as order 5. INFERRED: the body must be authored before the delegate decision at order 7, because that decision is whether to reuse THIS body.

sequence.action: on the Delegate Recipient step, either tick Use Primary Recipient Email or author a separate delegate body
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'If you want the primary recipient email and the delegate email to be the same, select (enable) the Use Primary Recipient Email check box.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). This is the one place the two-instance split can be collapsed; leave it clear and skip the delegate body and delegates receive the unedited stock text while the primary text looks correct.

sequence.action: decide whether the new text overwrites every language
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Yes if you would like to apply the new text to all languages.' (modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md). ORDER MATTERS BECAUSE IT IS DESTRUCTIVE ACROSS LOCALES - set it before saving edited text, since applying to all languages after per-language work has been done overwrites that work.

sequence.action: click Done to finish the notification
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the notification procedure ends 'Click Done.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). INFERRED: until the notification is committed it does not appear in the workflow General-page lists at orders 10-12.

sequence.action: open the workflow's General page and select the notification sent to the approver on submission
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED CROSS-TAB ORDERING, the crux of this whole procedure: 'Once the email notification is configured, the administrator assigns it to a workflow on the Workflows tab.' (overview-8b3df67d.md). The field itself: 'This notification is sent to the approver when the invoice is submitted by the employee.' (select-an-email-notification-in-the-workflows-tab-663bb8ac.md). Author-then-assign; a notification never assigned here never sends.

sequence.action: select the status-change notification
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This notification is sent to the submitter when the workflow status of the invoice changes.' (select-an-email-notification-in-the-workflows-tab-663bb8ac.md). Same author-then-assign ordering as order 10. CONTRADICTION IN THE CORPUS, carried not resolved: create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md presents Email Notifications as one General-page control, while 663bb8ac presents three separate per-slot selectors - a driver should expect either rendering.

sequence.action: select the sent-back notification
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This notification is sent to the submitter when the invoice is sent back to them.' (select-an-email-notification-in-the-workflows-tab-663bb8ac.md). NOTE recorded on this field in the roster: this notification is always sent and is not configurable on/off - only WHICH template is used is configurable here.

sequence.action: select the template used when an approval times out
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'When the time for approving an invoice has expired, the system can send out an expiration email to the approver' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md), and add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md states these copies exist precisely for this slot - 'These email notifications appear for use in Workflows when selecting an optional email notification template to send to an approver when a workflow step has timed out.' DEPENDS ON THE TIMEOUT LEG: with no Approval Time Expired Action set (grpworkflows-s1, order 10) there is no timeout to email about.

configSteps.name: Set the three exception-level thresholds on the Workflows Settings tab (invoice, purchase request, purchase order)
configSteps.goal: Documents carrying a severe enough exception are stopped before they move - an invoice cannot be submitted, a purchase request cannot be submitted, a purchase order cannot be transmitted. The threshold is a bare number and means nothing on its own: the exceptions and their levels must already exist, or the number blocks nothing and the configuration looks complete while being inert. Note that these three controls sit on three separate settings tables of the SAME Settings tab of the Workflows page - they are NOT the already-built 'Invoice Settings' page.

sequence.action: create the exception and give it a code, then set its level
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the Exceptions page's own documentation points forward at this very procedure: 'A workflow setting exists that prevents an invoice from being submitted if it has an exception of a certain level.' (add-exceptions-7b73d8f0.md). The level is defined here - 'Type any number between 0 and 99.' (same file). Set the Workflows threshold first and there is no exception at or above it, so nothing is ever blocked.

sequence.action: attach the exception to the rule that will raise it, confirming the level it carries
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the direction of the reference, not stated as a numbered sequence: an exception blocks submission only when something raises it, and the Audit Rules editor is where a defined exception is bound to a rule - 'It appears in the Exception Code, Exception Level, and Exception Text fields at the top of the page.' (add-a-custom-audit-rule-0f1d320e.md), i.e. the rule editor echoes the level defined at order 1. Skip this and the threshold is armed against an exception nothing ever generates.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, invoice settings table, type the level above which an invoice cannot be submitted
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type a number from one to 99. Any invoice that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the employee from submitting the invoice.' (invoice-settings-cace748d.md, a packed raw <table> row - a markdown-only parse misses it). CROSS-PAGE CONTRADICTION, recorded not reconciled: this file's range is 'one to 99' while the Exceptions page that defines the levels says 'Type any number between 0 and 99.' (add-exceptions-7b73d8f0.md). A level-0 exception can therefore be defined that this threshold cannot be set to match.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, purchase request settings table, type the level above which a PR cannot be submitted
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is a genuinely separate control rather than the same one relabelled: 'Type a number from one to 99. Any purchase request that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the employee from submitting the PR.' (purchase-request-settings-b0bce285.md). Setting only the invoice threshold leaves purchase requests unblocked - the classic half-configuration this step exists to prevent.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, purchase order settings table, type the level above which a PO cannot be transmitted
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and note the different verb - this one gates TRANSMISSION, not submission: 'Type a number from one to 99. Any purchase order that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the PO from being transmitted once it is created from its associated purchase request (PR).' (purchase-order-settings-a5a997b4.md). It fires later in the lifecycle than orders 3-4, so a PR that passed its own threshold can still stall here.

sequence.action: click Save on the Workflow Settings page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, with an explicit warning about immediacy: 'On the Workflow Settings page, select a setting option.' then Save, after which 'The system applies the setting immediately.' (enabling-and-disabling-an-invoice-workflow-setting-0e1e6d33.md). There is no staging - a threshold saved before the exceptions at orders 1-2 exist takes effect at once and blocks nothing, and a wrong number blocks live traffic the moment it is saved.

configSteps.name: Configure Cost Object Approval (hierarchy, then the workflow's Cost Object Hierarchy Type, then step order and self-approval)
configSteps.goal: Invoices route to the approver who owns the cost object they are charged to. The corpus orders this as define-hierarchy then activate-on-workflow then edit-steps, and each leg fails quietly on its own: the Cost Object Hierarchy Type list has nothing coherent to resolve without the hierarchy; the step order can violate a documented hard rule; and Allow Self Cost Object Approval is a check box that can be ticked with no effect at all unless Allow Self Approval is also on. Note the two legs sit behind DIFFERENT permissions.

sequence.action: select the Cost Object Approver hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as step 1 of the Cost Object Approval configuration, and explicitly generic: 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) - SAP publishes no COA-specific hierarchy procedure, so the generic Feature Hierarchies flow applies. ROLE GATE, quoted from the same file: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Feature Hierarchies section in Administration.'

sequence.action: click Modify Hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Modify Hierarchy.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md), the generic editor entry point that step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md defers to with 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.'

sequence.action: select the source list backing the cost object structure
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED prerequisite carried by the generic procedure: 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). The list is built in List Management, which is why that page precedes Feature Hierarchies in SAP's stated tool order (overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md).

sequence.action: add the level rows
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the generic instruction 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) combined with the two documented level behaviours - Employee, fixed, for Vendor Employee Access (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md) and Request for Invoice Payment (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). THE CORPUS DOES NOT STATE WHICH LEVEL VALUE THE COA HIERARCHY TAKES; do not assume either.

sequence.action: select the field acting as each hierarchy path segment
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED for the generic editor: 'In the Segment Name list, select the field that will act as the list in User Permissions' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED for COA specifically, via 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) - the segments are what an invoice's cost object values are matched against, so a hierarchy with no segments resolves no approver.

sequence.action: click Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). This save is the boundary: order 7 is titled 'Step 2: Activate the Feature' precisely because the hierarchy is Step 1.

sequence.action: from the Invoice Processing Admin menu open Workflows, then select the workflow and click Modify (or Copy to create a new one)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Modify an existing workflow by selecting it and clicking Modify (or double-click the desired workflow).' (step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md). ROLE GATE, quoted from the same file and DIFFERENT from order 1's: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Workflows section in Administration.' - one operator may be able to do the hierarchy leg and not this one.

sequence.action: on the General page set the Cost Object Hierarchy Type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Cost Object Hierarchy Type field, select the desired type: Level or Limit.' (step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md), which is the topic SAP titles 'Step 2: Activate the Feature' - the activation is this field, not a separate switch. The same file adds the conditional follow-on: '(Optional) If Limit is selected, you can also select Cost Object Hierarchy Type to route the cost object _directly_ to that approver with the required approval limit amount.'

sequence.action: click Next to reach the Steps page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Next. The Steps page appears (see next section).' (step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md). The Steps page is reachable only through the wizard on an opened workflow, so the General-page value at order 8 is necessarily committed first.

sequence.action: reorder the workflow steps so the Cost Object Approval step sits correctly
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD RULE, and the one thing in this procedure that produces an invalid workflow rather than an inert one: 'The Vendor Approval system step _cannot_ precede the Cost Object Approval step.' (step-3-edit-the-workflow-steps-f2731590.md). The same file gives the default placement to reason from: 'By default, the new workflow step appears in the workflow just prior to the Prepayment Validation step.'

sequence.action: on the General page enable Allow Self Approval
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED MASTER GATE that must precede order 12: 'This feature will only work if the Allow Self Approval option is also selected (enabled).' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md, of Allow Self Cost Object Approval). Tick the cost-object option alone and it is saved, displayed as on, and does nothing - the textbook silent half-configuration. The same file gates a second control the same way: 'The Allow Self Approval option must be enabled (checked) in order for the Allow Invoice Processor to Process their own Invoices option to work.'

sequence.action: enable Allow Self Cost Object Approval
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Allows the cost object approver to approve invoices regardless of whether they are the owner of the invoice or not.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md), subject to the master gate quoted at order 11. DOCUMENTED NON-INTERACTION worth knowing here: 'The _prompt for approver_ setting has no affect within the cost object approval step.' (additional-approver-situations-fbb5034c.md) - do not expect the own-approver Settings control to influence this step.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, decide whether cost object approvers see only their own line items
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'When selected, filters a Cost Object Approver's view to only those cost object line items and amount totals that apply to that approver; all others are removed from view.' (invoice-settings-cace748d.md, packed raw <table> row). INFERRED ordering: it is a Settings-tab control that applies globally, so it changes what EVERY cost object approver on every workflow sees - set it once, deliberately, after the workflow-level legs, and note enabling-and-disabling-an-invoice-workflow-setting-0e1e6d33.md's warning that 'The system applies the setting immediately.'

configSteps.name: Create a confirmation agreement and put it in force on submit and approve actions
configSteps.goal: Users and approvers must accept a legal disclaimer at submit and/or approve time. The corpus states the chain in one sentence - create, associate to the workflow, associate the workflow to the policy - and every link is required: an agreement with no workflow association never renders, and a workflow with no policy association is never used, so the agreement appears configured and no user ever sees it.

sequence.action: on the Confirmation Agreements tab click New and enter a unique internal name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this is link 1 of the chain SAP states in one sentence: 'After creating the agreement, you associate the confirmation agreement with the workflow, and then associate the workflow with the policy.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). The name is internal only - 'This name is used internally in the workflow; the user or approver cannot see this.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md) - so it is what the General-page lists at orders 6-7 match on, and must be distinctive enough to pick correctly there.

sequence.action: enter the title shown in bold above the message body
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'The text that is typed here appears in bold (no HTML tagging is required) and appears at the top of the message body area, directly below the title bar.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md). Unlike the name at order 1, THIS is what users see - conflating the two produces an agreement whose visible heading is an internal code.

sequence.action: enter the agreement text
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD LIMIT that constrains drafting before it constrains configuration: 'You may type up to 2000 characters.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md). The same row enumerates the HTML tags permitted inside this free-text field - those are markup allowed in the body, NOT selectable values for the control.

sequence.action: select the groups permitted to edit the agreement
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the group or groups that can edit the agreement.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md). LABEL CASING TO EXPECT, verbatim from the corpus: this control is labelled 'Editable by Group(s)' with a lower-case 'by', unlike the General-page 'Editable By Group(s)' - a driver matching on exact label text must carry both forms.

sequence.action: save the Confirmation Agreement window
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the create-then-associate ordering stated at activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md ('After creating the agreement, you associate the confirmation agreement with the workflow'): the object must be committed before the workflow's General-page lists can offer it. Save is the shared commit control across the object-edit dialogs on this page.

sequence.action: open the workflow's General page and choose the agreement shown on submit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, link 2 of the chain: 'In the Submit Confirmation Agreement list, choose the agreement to be displayed when submitting the invoice.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). The list is populated from the Confirmation Agreements tab objects, so running this before orders 1-5 offers nothing to choose.

sequence.action: choose the agreement shown on approval actions
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and a genuinely separate slot: 'In the Approval Confirmation Agreement list, choose the agreement to be displayed when approving the invoice.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). Setting only the submit slot leaves approvers with no confirmation at all - the half-works case for this procedure.

sequence.action: click Done to commit the workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the association procedure ends 'Click Done.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). INFERRED: the workflow must be committed before the policy at order 9 binds to the version carrying these two selections.

sequence.action: open the policy and select this workflow, then save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, link 3 and the reason the whole chain can silently do nothing: 'then associate the workflow with the policy.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). LABEL DRIFT IN THE SOURCE, recorded verbatim rather than smoothed: the same file's procedure says 'In the Expense Report Workflow list, choose the appropriate workflow.' while the built Policies page carries this control as Invoice Workflow - two labels in the corpus for the same association.

sequence.action: save the policy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). ONE-WAY DOOR: after this save the workflow is assigned, and 'The system does not allow you to delete a workflow that is currently assigned to a policy.' (delete-a-workflow-or-workflow-steps-e9a84a07.md).

configSteps.name: Set one approver's authorization limit in the Authorized Approval Limits window (hierarchy branch)
configSteps.goal: Give one named approver the signing authority a non-PO invoice has nowhere else to get it from: a PO-based invoice carries its approval authority on the purchase order, a non-PO invoice carries none, so this per-approver limit IS the authority (tools-guides/workflow-and-approval-routing-8b4ff6c9.md: 'All workflow options available for non-PO policies are also available to a PO-based invoice policy. This includes options such as workflow rules and Authorized Approvers.'). WHAT SILENTLY HALF-WORKS IF A LEG IS SKIPPED. (a) Skip the activation or hierarchy legs and the Authorized Approval Limits link is simply absent from User Administration - the driver finds no window at all and, if the hierarchy is Global-only, finds the branch-A inline check box instead (that is step grpapproval-authority-s2-global-group-only-inline-limit, a different control set). (b) Skip the left-side hierarchy level selection and every right-side value is written against whichever level the window opens on. (c) Set Can approve exception without the tenant-wide min/max exception range on Workflows and the approver holds an exception right with no band to exercise it in. (d) Complete BOTH the Approval Limit area and the Level field and the system honours only the one matching the cost object configuration and silently ignores the other - a populated field is NOT evidence the field is in effect. (e) The two value semantics a driver will otherwise get backwards: 0 puts the approver in the chain with NO final authority, blank/null means UNLIMITED. HONEST COVERAGE GAP, stated rather than invented: no corpus file documents a Save, Cancel or Done button for this window itself (branch A documents a Save click, branch B does not), so no commit control is emitted here and a driver must discover it at runtime.

sequence.action: confirm (or set) the Authorized Approver feature activation on the Authorized Approvers tab > Configuration sub-tab - this is a PRECONDITION CHECK for this procedure, not a re-authoring of the activation itself
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD PRECONDITION - without it the page this step targets does not render at all: 'If the Authorized Approver feature is activated and the company's Authorized Approver hierarchy has at least one level (in addition to Global), then the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). The activation act itself is quoted at 'To activate the feature, select Authorized Approver feature is available for workflows.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/procedure-2d20b513.md) and is already fully authored as orders 13-15 of grpworkflows-s2-configure-authorized-approver-feature; it appears here ONLY as the precondition leg, and a driver should run that step rather than duplicate it. CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED - the two guide threads name DIFFERENT features as the gate on the same link: the Cost Object Approval thread says 'When the Cost Object Approver feature is activated, the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Settings section in User Administration.' and then, in its own Note, ALSO restates the Authorized-Approver condition - 'To view the Authorized Approval Limits link, you need to have activated the Authorized Approver feature and the company’s Authorized Approver hierarchy needs to have at least on level (in addition to Global).' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/user-administration-8b167b96.md; SAP's typo 'at least on level' preserved verbatim). So one file names one feature and the other internally names both. Check BOTH features before concluding the link should be visible; do not pick a winner. NOTE the Cost Object Approver feature activation has no built page in this graph and is a legitimately open forward reference.

sequence.action: confirm the Authorized Approver hierarchy carries at least one level in addition to Global - again a PRECONDITION CHECK; building the hierarchy is grpworkflows-s2-configure-authorized-approver-feature orders 1-12
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, AND IT IS THIS LEG THAT SELECTS WHICH BRANCH OF THE PAGE EXISTS. Same sentence as order 1 supplies the level condition: 'the company's Authorized Approver hierarchy has at least one level (in addition to Global), then the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). The opposite shape produces a DIFFERENT control set, not a degraded one: 'If the Authorized Approver feature is activated and the company has only one group (Global), then the Authorized Approver check box appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section in Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.' (same file) - that is the mutually exclusive branch handled by grpapproval-authority-s2-global-group-only-inline-limit. The configuration matrix marks the hierarchy leg as its own numbered step - 'Create a connected (multi-level) list of the hierarchy levels.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md). INFERRED: a driver must determine hierarchy shape ONCE, before navigating, and then commit to exactly one branch's controls - running the wrong branch means hunting for controls that cannot be on screen.

sequence.action: in User Administration, with the approver's user record loaded, click the Authorized Approval Limits link in the Expense and Invoices Settings section to open the window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and given as numbered step 1 of SAP's own sequence: 'In the Expense and Invoices Settings section of User Administration, click the Authorized Approval Limits link.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/user-administration-8b167b96.md), corroborated by 'The administrator clicks the link. The Authorized Approval Limits window appears.' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). NAVIGATION FACT A DRIVER MUST CARRY: this window is reached through Administration > COMPANY, not through Administration > Invoice - 'Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration' (fcfd570c) - so the Invoice Processing Admin middle nav node that most Invoice admin pages hang off does not apply here. ROLE GATE, quoted, THREE conditions of which the third is about the record being edited rather than the operator: 'To see the link described here, the administrator must have the User Admin rights and the Invoice User Administration rights. In addition, the employee must be an approver.' (fcfd570c). A driver holding only User Admin, or pointed at a non-approver employee, will find the link missing and must not conclude the feature is off.

sequence.action: on the left side of the window, select the hierarchy level this limit is being granted at
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED ORDERING, numbered explicitly as step 2 ahead of the right-side values at step 3: 'On the left side, select the appropriate level in the hierarchy.' (user-administration-8b167b96.md), independently attested as 'On the left side, the administrator selects the appropriate level in the hierarchy.' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). INFERRED consequence of running out of order: the right-side controls are read against whatever level is currently selected, so entering a currency and amount first writes the authorization to the window's default level rather than the intended one - and nothing on screen reports the mismatch. DOCUMENTARY GAP, stated plainly: neither file gives this control an on-screen caption; both describe only the ACTION, so a driver must locate it positionally (left pane) rather than by label text.

sequence.action: on the right side, select the Can approve exception check box if this approver is an exception approver
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is the first of the right-side bullets in fcfd570c: 'For exception approvers, the administrator selects the Can approve exception check box. (The actual exception levels apply to all authorized approvers and are defined on the Authorized Approvers tab in Workflows.)'. THAT PARENTHETICAL IS THE SCOPE FENCE AND THE ORDERING RULE AT ONCE: what is set HERE is a per-approver boolean; the band it operates in is tenant-wide and lives on the already-built Workflows page as field.workflows.minimum-exception-level and field.workflows.maximum-exception-level. Corroborated from a second file and a second guide thread: 'The range is set in Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Authorized Approver tab.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configuration-8b3be88b.md). INFERRED from those two: tick this box before that range exists and the approver holds an exception right with no band to exercise - the record saves clean and the authority is inert. NOTE for a driver reading the graph: the identically-labelled field.workflows.authorized-approver-can-approve-exception is a SIBLING control on a different surface writing the same underlying per-approver record - 'Regardless of how the authorized approvers are entered into Invoice, they all appear in the Authorized Approver List.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md) - so setting it in both places is redundant, not additive. TAB-NAME DRIFT to expect at runtime: fcfd570c writes 'Authorized Approvers tab', 8b3be88b writes 'Authorized Approver tab' for the same Workflows tab.

sequence.action: in the Approval Limit area on the right side, select the currency for this approver's limit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the currency-then-amount order is the order both primaries state: 'For limit approvers, the administrator selects the desired currency and enters the amount.' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md) and 'For limit-based cost object approval, select a currency and enter an amount.' (user-administration-8b167b96.md). INFERRED requiredness, from the import surface only: the employee-import record set 710 field table makes the currency conditionally required by the amount - 'If used, then Approval Limit Currency Code below is required.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/employee-import-e28f2294.md) - cited for the value domain and pairing rule, NOT as documentation of this window's own controls; neither primary states a requiredness rule for the window. DOCUMENTARY GAP: this branch's currency control is UNCAPTIONED in every file that describes it, unlike the Global-group branch whose counterpart is named outright as 'the Approval Limit Currency list' - do not search this window for that caption.

sequence.action: enter the limit amount, or leave it blank for unlimited authority, or enter 0 for chain-membership without final authority
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED VALUE SEMANTICS - the two a driver gets backwards, both quoted. ZERO: 'You can enter 0 in the Amount field.' and, in the same paragraph, 'This puts the approver into the authorized approver workflow but will prevent that approver from having final authority to approve the invoice.' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md); stated a second way by the other primary - 'To include an approver in the COA approval chain so users can see/approve an invoice, but not have signing authority for any amount in the cost center, enter zero (0).' (user-administration-8b167b96.md). BLANK: 'For an unlimited approval amount, leave blank (null).' (user-administration-8b167b96.md), corroborated surface-agnostically by 'a limit amount of null will result in an unlimited approval/no limit approval amount.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/setting-an-unlimited-approval-amount-9d98b489.md). SO 0 AND BLANK ARE OPPOSITE ENDS OF THE AUTHORITY SCALE, NOT SYNONYMS FOR 'nothing set'. CONTRADICTION, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED, and it bites exactly on the unlimited case: this window and 9d98b489 each state a ONE-act recipe (blank the amount), while the Workflows sibling surface requires TWO acts - 'set to no approval limit currency, and leave the approval limit amount blank' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md, cited here for boundary reasoning only, never as a source for this page). Whether the currency must ALSO be cleared on THIS window is UNDETERMINED by the documentation; leave the amount blank per the two files that describe this surface, and only clear the currency as well if a live check shows the amount alone is insufficient. NOTE: Workflows carries a sibling control for this same underlying value as field.workflows.authorized-approver-approval-limit, labelled 'Approval Limit', which collapses currency and amount into one record where this window presents two.

sequence.action: for level-based cost object approval, select the level - IF the control is present on this window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED PRECEDENCE RULE, the single most consequential sentence on this page and the reason this entry comes AFTER orders 6-7 rather than instead of them: 'The cost object configuration defines the type—either limit or level. If you complete both areas in this window—the Approval Limit area and the Level field—Concur Invoice will use the one that applies to your configuration and ignore the other.' (user-administration-8b167b96.md; three em dashes - the ASCII-hyphen form does not exist in the file). The cost object configuration is set ELSEWHERE, so a driver cannot read this window to learn which of its own values is live: completing both is permitted, and one of them is silently discarded. The act itself: 'For level-based cost object approval, select a level.' (same file). CONTESTED EXISTENCE, OPEN CONTRADICTION - a driver must not assume this control renders: 'Levels cannot be added to approvers via User Administration.' and 'The levels can be added to users via the Employee Import or the Authorized Approver list (Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Authorized Approver tab).' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/filter-authorized-approvers-by-workflow-approval-step-aae69350.md), reinforced by the very topic that supplies the three-setter rule - 'If you are assigning "levels" to authorized approvers, refer to Filter Authorized Approvers by Workflow Approval Step in this guide.' (step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md). FALLBACK IF ABSENT AT RUNTIME: set the level through the Employee Import or through the Authorized Approver List on the already-built Workflows page. HYPOTHESIS ONLY, not adopted: the two files may describe two different values sharing one label - aae69350's Level is the authorized-approver workflow-step filter (built as field.workflows.authorized-approver-level), while 8b167b96's is the level-based COST OBJECT approval level. Because of that, never treat cost_object_approval_level and field.workflows.authorized-approver-level as interchangeable targets for one driver action.

configSteps.name: Set a manager approval limit inline when the company has the Global group only (the window does not exist)
configSteps.goal: Grant limit approval authority to an approver at a site whose Authorized Approver hierarchy carries nothing but Global. This is the MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ALTERNATIVE to grpapproval-authority-s1-set-one-approver-authorization-limit, not a shorter version of it: in this configuration the Authorized Approval Limits link and window DO NOT EXIST and an inline check box on the user record is the entire control surface. WHAT SILENTLY HALF-WORKS. (a) The whole method is LIMIT-ONLY - there is no Can approve exception control on this branch, so a site that needs exception-based authorized approvers cannot get them here and must build a non-Global hierarchy level first, which flips the surface to branch B. (b) The two limit fields do not exist until the check box is selected, so a driver that goes looking for them first finds nothing and may wrongly conclude the feature is off. (c) Zero and blank carry the same opposite semantics as on branch B - 0 means in the chain with no final authority. (d) This is one of three interchangeable surfaces writing one underlying per-approver record, so doing it here AND on the Workflows Authorized Approver List is redundant, not additive.

sequence.action: confirm the Authorized Approver feature is activated on the Authorized Approvers tab > Configuration sub-tab - a PRECONDITION CHECK, authored in full as grpworkflows-s2-configure-authorized-approver-feature order 13
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the gate applies to THIS branch just as much as to the hierarchy branch: 'If the Authorized Approver feature is activated and the company has only one group (Global), then the Authorized Approver check box appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section in Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). The two-column configuration matrix marks the activation step in BOTH deployment columns - 'Activate the Authorized Approver feature:' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md) - which is precisely why this leg is not skippable on the Global-group-only path. INFERRED, and it is the branch selector: do NOT also add a non-Global hierarchy level while intending to use this branch. The corpus states the two renderings differ by hierarchy shape - 'The settings that appear in User Administration (Administration > User Administration) differ depending on whether the configuration includes:' (fcfd570c) - so adding a level converts this surface into the Authorized Approval Limits window and the inline check box ceases to be the place to work.

sequence.action: with the approver's user record loaded in User Administration, select the Authorized Approver check box in the Expense and Invoices Setting section
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and it is a REVEAL, which is why nothing can be entered before it: 'When the administrator selects the check box, the Manager Approval Limit field and the Approval Limit Currency list appear.' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). SCOPE LIMIT, corpus-stated and load-bearing for choosing this procedure at all: 'This method is used only for limit-based authorized approvers. It cannot be used for exception-based authorized approvers.' (same file) - if the requirement is exception-based approval this step is the wrong one and cannot be made to work. ROLE GATE, quoted, and note it is a TWO-condition gate here where branch B has three: 'In order to see the check box described here, the user must have the User Admin rights and the Invoice User Administration rights.' (same file). NAVIGATION FACT: like branch B this is reached through Administration > COMPANY - 'Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration' - never through Administration > Invoice.

sequence.action: select the currency in the Approval Limit Currency list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as one of the two controls the check box reveals, and named with an actual on-screen caption unlike its branch-B counterpart: 'the Manager Approval Limit field and the Approval Limit Currency list appear.' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). INFERRED ordering, from the branch-B wording of the same pairing ('the administrator selects the desired currency and enters the amount', same file): currency then amount. The currency value domain is not enumerated on this surface anywhere in the corpus; the only documented domain for the pair is on the employee-import 710 record set - 'Can be either three-digit or three-letter currency code; must be a valid currency in the list of system (reimbursement) currencies' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/employee-import-e28f2294.md) - cited for context only, and the import itself defers to an external Shared specification absent from this corpus.

sequence.action: enter the limit in the Manager Approval Limit field (or 0 for chain membership without final authority), then click Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, including the Save that closes this branch - branch A is the only one of the two for which a commit click is documented at all: 'The administrator makes the appropriate choices and clicks Save.' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). ZERO SEMANTICS, quoted against THIS label specifically: 'You can enter 0 in the Manager Approval Limit field. This puts the approver into the authorized approver workflow but will prevent that approver from having final authority to approve the invoice (cannot limit-approve).' (same file) - the '(cannot limit-approve)' parenthetical belongs to this branch-A label and to no other, do not carry it onto the branch-B Amount field. UNLIMITED/NULL: NOT separately attested against this label. concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/setting-an-unlimited-approval-amount-9d98b489.md is surface-agnostic ('a limit amount of null will result in an unlimited approval/no limit approval amount.') and applies here only by extension - flagged as INFERRED, not corpus-stated for 'Manager Approval Limit' by name. REDUNDANCY WARNING, corpus-stated: 'Regardless of how the authorized approvers are entered into Invoice, they all appear in the Authorized Approver List.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md) - this value, field.workflows.authorized-approver-approval-limit on the built Workflows page, and the employee import are three surfaces onto ONE record, so a driver should pick one and not reconcile three.

configValueSets.context: READING A of the Life to Date tolerance refinement - the THREE options step-2 offers after a Life to Date check box is selected. Conditional on the check box, and the three are NOT flat alternatives: the source binds Value and Currency with '- AND -' and separates that pair from Percentage with '- OR -'.
configValueSets.sourceQuote: As you select each check box, options appear that let you refine the tolerance.
configValueSets.notes: CONTRADICTS READING B (the next set), which is the same control on the same tab labelled 'Overage Tolerance' with only two options and no Currency. NOT RECONCILED - both are emitted. Step-2 never gives this section a label at all; the label 'Overage Tolerance' exists only in configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md, which is why the roster field is named overage_tolerance and why attaching Reading A here is a wiring decision, not a corpus claim. Verbatim option text: Value = 'Specify a number at or above that at which the rule set will trigger an exception. For example, if the Value is 100 and the PO amount is 1000, invoice(s) at or above 1100 will trigger the exception.'; Currency = 'Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system.'; Percentage = 'Choose a percent above which the rule set will trigger a flag. For example, if the Percentage is 1 and the PO amount is 1000, invoice(s) above 1010 will trigger the exception.' configValueSets.context: The 6-term terminology glossary for this page's objects, published as a bullet run.
values: Concur Receiving: The ability for users to add quantity receipt data manually in Concur Invoice.
Purchase Order Payment Request: An invoice associated with a PO by the unique number associated with the PO.
Life to Date: The complete span of all invoices associated with their purchase order.
Associate: The relationship created when an invoice is linked to a PO by entering the unique PO number in the request header form.
Matching Rule Set: The combination of rules that is executed for every PO request matched under a given policy.
Named Rules Group: Any rule existing within ("under") the Matching Rule Set, for example, a condition-based rule group.
configValueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: A glossary is not a field's option list. These are the authoritative object names for the page's node graph, not values an admin selects. Anchoring quote: 'The following terms are used throughout this document and within Invoice.' All six terms, verbatim and complete, in source order; the Matching Rule Set entry is cut at its first sentence, the source continuing 'Can be a simple, single rule, or more complex multiple match rule that includes "nested" condition-based rules run against custom fields that differentiate by spend type, project, or division as examples.' TERMINOLOGY TENSION worth flagging for a driver: 'Life to Date' is simultaneously a glossary concept, a tab name (life_to_date_tab) and a rule-type value (matching_rule_type), so a text match on those three words is ambiguous. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A glossary or vocabulary node type in the schema. It should never be wired to a field.

configValueSets.context: The complete data-variable catalog that may be typed into an email body. A STRUCTURED catalog, not a picker: every row of the source table yields a LABEL form and a VALUE form of one variable, and the label form is the value form with 'L_' inserted after the opening percent sign.
configValueSets.sourceQuote: Field Label: %L\_WhoChanged%
configValueSets.notes: ALL 18 DISTINCT VARIABLES, IN SOURCE ORDER, NONE SAMPLED. ESCAPING - A DELIBERATE, FLAGGED TRANSCRIPTION DECISION: the markdown source writes every underscore escaped as backslash-underscore (the sourceQuote above preserves that exactly, which is why it reads '%L\_WhoChanged%'), but the backslash is markdown escaping, not a character of the variable. The values array therefore carries the UNESCAPED strings a user actually types, which is what the automation needs. STRUCTURE: eleven table rows in two labelled sections - 'Invoice or Purchase Request Change' (Changed By, Request Name*, Request Date, Submit Date, Total Amount, Approval Status of the Workflow Step, Pay Status = 7 rows) and 'Invoice or Purchase Request Pending Approval' (Report From, Report From, Request Name, Total = 4 rows). Eleven rows yield 18 rather than 22 distinct variables because %L_RequestName%/%RequestName% and %L_Total%/%Total% appear in BOTH sections; and two different rows share the Field label 'Report From' while carrying DIFFERENT variables (%EmpName% = 'The name of the user who owns the invoice', %SubmittingUserName% = 'The name of the user who submitted the invoice'). The asterisk on 'Request Name*' resolves to the table's own footer row, which the markdown escapes the leading asterisk of: '\*These fields use the configured form field label, if available, instead of the default label.' SEMANTICS from general-information-00eca1ce.md: 'The variables are enclosed in percentage signs, which indicate to the system that they need to be replaced.', 'Adding an “L” (L) and underscore (\_) to the beginning of the variable name tells the system to replace that variable with the field label.', and 'NOTE: If the variable is blank, then both label and value variables will not print in the resulting email.' DO NOT SOURCE THIS CATALOG FROM email-notifications-8b3dbad4.md, which is a 61-row revision history containing exactly one variable. MARKDOWN ESCAPE, documented 2026-08-31 (Workflows correctness critic): 9 of these 18 values will not verify as literal substrings of the cited file, because the corpus escapes the underscore for markdown - the file writes "%L\_WhoChanged%" and this set records "%L_WhoChanged%". The UNESCAPED form is correct for the graph: a driver typing into an email template types %L_WhoChanged%, and the backslash is markdown syntax, not part of the variable. The catalog itself is COMPLETE and verified - all 18 variables (9 %L\_X% label forms and 9 %X% value forms) are genuinely present in the file; nothing was inferred from the documented "add L and underscore" rule. The value-set-entries-not-in-file WARN on these two sets is therefore expected and accepted, not a regression.

configContradictions.topic: The tab that groups expense types under a tax authority is written 'Expense Types Group' and 'Expense Type Groups' inside one and the same topic, and only 'Expense Type Groups' in three others.

readings.summary: The process overview names the tab 'Expense Type Groups' (plural Groups) inside the full Administration menu path.
readings.sourceQuote: Administration > Invoice > Tax Administration > Expense Type Groups tab

readings.summary: The step-by-step procedure that actually drives the tab names it 'Expense Types Group' (plural Types, singular Group).
readings.sourceQuote: On the Expense Types Group tab, select from the Tax Authority list.

readings.summary: The very topic that wrote 'Expense Types Group' in its first numbered step writes 'Expense Type Groups' later in its own Applies To note - so the drift is inside a single topic, not only between topics.
readings.sourceQuote: The Applies To setting also appears as a column on the Expense Type Groups page.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe the Tax Administration tab strip for 'Expense Type Groups' FIRST - that is the form four separate files use - and accept 'Expense Types Group' only as a fallback if the primary probe finds nothing. The two are not coequal candidates, so do not 'take whichever resolves first'. A normalised match on the tokens expense/type/group (case-insensitive, tolerant of where the plural s falls) is the safe locator; never hard-match one literal string and fail. Record the literal text seen so later steps reuse the observed string rather than a guessed one.
configContradictions.notes: Corpus weight: 'Expense Type Groups' occurs in four files (apply-vat-to-expense-type-groups-0efbc573, step-5-optional-add-a-new-expense-type-group-to-a-tax-authority-e8d87361, step-6-optional-add-a-new-vendor-group-to-a-tax-authority-d8b7786d, the-basic-process-12a5686d) while 'Expense Types Group' occurs in exactly one (e8d87361). Hypothesis: the singular-Group form is a transcription slip in a single numbered step. The alternative explanation - that the tab was renamed between releases and only one topic was updated - is ruled out by the corpus itself, because e8d87361 carries BOTH spellings, so the two forms demonstrably coexisted in one document at one time.

The lone occurrence also self-corrects inside its own sentence, naming the destination 'the Tax Administration tool', which is why 'Tax Administrator' is recorded as the fallback rather than as a coequal name. configContradictions.topic: The role is written 'Invoice Tax Administrator' wherever a topic quotes the Available Roles list, and plain 'Tax Administrator' in prose, in step titles and in the required-roles topic.

configContradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW. The corpus arguably shows the short form is shorthand rather than a competing list entry: both Step 2 topics are titled with the short form yet instruct selecting the long one from Available Roles (b7f391c8 'Under Available Roles, select Invoice Tax Administrator, then click Add.', and b903b7c8 line 33 'In the Available Roles list, select Invoice Tax Administrator, and then click Add.'), and no topic anywhere claims the list contains a literal entry 'Tax Administrator'. This node is therefore NOT a claim that two roles exist. Drive to the User Permissions screen by trying, in order, the top menu entries 'Administration > Company > Company Admin', 'User Administration', and 'User Admin', then look for a 'User Permissions' left-menu item; treat arrival at a screen that offers an Invoice tab plus an Available Roles list as the success condition.

configContradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW. The two topics may simply be naming the field and the value it holds rather than disagreeing: 14c3ef13 gives the label with the description 'This is the unique account number provided by a tax service provider to the client', which is what c3fe1df5's activity name describes typing. The List Management half of that topic ('Invoice Admin or Invoice: Using the List Management tool to create a new list category (or use an existing one) and create a new list within the category') says nothing about where definitions are authored and is recorded here rather than as a reading. The role half overlaps the List Management roles node; the two were not merged because they gate different surfaces. The alternative - that a genuinely separate surface is visible only to sites provisioned with Shared Configuration administration - is also only a hypothesis; the corpus never reconciles the two accounts.

The genuine disagreement is the admin guides' 'Invoice Admin' against the tools guides' 'Invoice Configuration Administrator' for the same tool, the latter generalised over Step 1 List Management by overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md.
