Hypothesis, not a finding: the two are different fields - the Exceptions page assigns a LEVEL to an exception (where 0 is a legitimate non-urgent level) while the Settings-tab controls set a THRESHOLD above which submission or transmission is blocked, for which 0 would block everything. That would make both statements locally correct. The corpus never says so, so the discrepancy is recorded rather than explained away. This is a CROSS-PAGE contradiction: it touches the built Exceptions page and must not be resolved by editing that page.

configContradictions.topic: The Role value list differs between the Add Workflow Step field description and the shipped default workflows: the field description names System plus five non-system roles and omits Employee, while both shipped workflows use Employee as the Role of step 1.

readings.summary: The Add Workflow Step field table names five non-system roles after 'such as', and does NOT include Employee.
readings.sourceQuote: If it is a non-system role, such as Authorized Approver, Invoice Approver, Invoice Processor, Invoice Processor Manager, or Invoice Vendor Manager, then you must select an action or multiple actions in the Approval Actions field.

readings.summary: The default-workflow tables define a Role column for the shipped workflows, whose step 1 Role is Employee - a value the field description never lists.
readings.sourceQuote: In the table below, the Role column defines the type of user that takes action at this step.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Treat the Role list as OPEN, not closed - the field description hedges with 'such as', so it is explicitly not an enumeration. Expect at least seven candidates (System, Employee, Authorized Approver, Invoice Approver, Invoice Processor, Invoice Processor Manager, Invoice Vendor Manager) and READ the live dropdown rather than asserting a fixed set. Do not emit a value set for this field from the 'such as' sentence.
configContradictions.notes: Hypothesis: Employee is the role of the submission step only and may be system-assigned rather than selectable, which would explain its absence from the field description. The corpus does not say so, so this is carried as a genuine disagreement. Note the practical asymmetry: an over-narrow list here would make a driver reject a legitimate value, which is worse than leaving the list open.

configContradictions.topic: The Default PO Payment Workflow is documented with two steps in one guide and seven in another.

readings.summary: The Default Workflows topic calls the PO workflow 'very simple' and lists exactly two default steps.
readings.sourceQuote: Default PO Payment Workflow: This workflow by default is very simple. The default steps are:

readings.summary: The purchase-order guide enumerates seven steps for the same named workflow, including steps the other list lacks entirely.
readings.sourceQuote: As an example, the workflow for the Default PO Payment Workflow included in Concur Invoice is:

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Never assume the shipped PO workflow's shape. Read the actual Steps page before copying or reordering it. If the driver must reason about it, treat the seven-step list as the superset - it contains the mandatory system steps the two-step list omits.
configContradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the two-step table lists only the CONFIGURABLE steps and silently omits the mandatory system steps, while the seven-step list includes them and tags them '(system step)'. That would reconcile the two - but the corpus never says so, and the two-step table DOES include system steps for the other default workflow, which undercuts the hypothesis. Recorded unreconciled.

configContradictions.topic: The set of steps every workflow must contain is stated as at least three, then bulleted as four named steps, and contradicted by a shipped workflow that has two.

readings.summary: The Required Steps topic says at least three, then bullets four named steps.
readings.sourceQuote: An invoice workflow always consists of at least three steps, but additional steps may be added:

readings.summary: The shipped Default PO Payment Workflow contains only two steps, none of them the named required ones.
readings.sourceQuote: Default PO Payment Workflow: This workflow by default is very simple. The default steps are:

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not encode a minimum step count and do not pre-validate a workflow against one. Before removing any step, attempt the removal and read the UI's own gating - the corpus offers no more reliable signal than the Remove button becoming available.
configContradictions.notes: Kept separate from the PO-workflow step-count contradiction because the claim is different: that one is about how many steps a NAMED shipped workflow has, this one about how many steps ANY workflow must have. They share one reading, which is deliberate - the two-step shipped workflow is the counter-example in both. Hypotheses: the 'at least three' sentence is stale and was not updated when a fourth step joined the list; and/or the PO workflow table is abridged. Both are hypotheses.

configContradictions.topic: The page itself is named singular and plural in two consecutive sentences of one file: 'the Workflow page' and 'the Workflows page'.

readings.summary: Singular: 'On the Workflow page, admin will see the Require Hardcopy Receipts option.'
readings.sourceQuote: On the Workflow page, admin will see the Require Hardcopy Receipts option.

readings.summary: Plural, in the very next sentence of the same file.
readings.sourceQuote: the Require Hardcopy Receipts option on the Workflows page

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Match the page and its tabs on a case-insensitive prefix 'Workflow' and never gate an automation on the trailing 's'. The same singular/plural drift affects the Workflow(s) tab, Email Notification(s), Confirmation Agreement(s) and Authorized Approver(s) - it is a corpus-wide pattern on this page.
configContradictions.notes: The two readings cite the SAME file and different quotes, deliberately: this contradiction exists only inside one file, which is what makes it evidence of editorial inconsistency rather than of two surfaces. Distinct from the Workflows-tab drift (recorded separately), which is about the tab and spans fourteen files against one. Hypothesis: pure editorial inconsistency.

configContradictions.topic: What value the Level control takes on a feature hierarchy, and whether it can be changed at all: 'Employee', stated as the default and unchangeable, versus 'Request', which the administrator sets.

readings.summary: For the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy, Level is Employee and the topic states outright that it is the default and cannot be changed.
readings.sourceQuote: Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).

readings.summary: For the Invoice Payment feature hierarchy, the same New-row step SETS the level, and sets it to Request - an act of choosing, with no immutability claim and no mention of Employee.
readings.sourceQuote: Set the level to Request.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do NOT hardcode a Level option list and do NOT assume the control is editable or read-only. Branch on the feature hierarchy already selected: under Invoice Vendor Employee Access expect Employee pre-filled and accept it without writing; under Invoice Payment expect to set Request explicitly. For any OTHER feature hierarchy the corpus documents no Level value at all - read the offered options at runtime and report them rather than guessing, and never carry a value across from one feature hierarchy to another.
configContradictions.notes: Raised by all three lenses with identical readings. HYPOTHESIS, not established: Level is feature-scoped, each feature hierarchy declaring which entity its levels hang off, so both topics are locally correct about different provisioning. A COMPETING hypothesis that cannot be excluded from documentation alone: 'Level' means different things on the two screens - a row-type selector in one, a hierarchy tier ordinal in the other - which would make this label drift rather than an option-list conflict. A third data point resolves neither: understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md says the Request Authorized Approver hierarchy uses the Request and Employee fields - BOTH names, in a third feature hierarchy. Neither hypothesis is testable without a tenant, and this build has none.

configContradictions.topic: Whether the left-menu entry under Administration > Invoice reads 'Feature Hierarchies' or plain 'Hierarchies'.

readings.summary: The only topic corpus-wide that documents the actual left-menu click writes the label as Feature Hierarchies.
readings.sourceQuote: Click Feature Hierarchies (left menu).

readings.summary: The dedicated Hierarchies topic writes the same menu destination as bare Hierarchies, with 'Feature' absent from both its title and its navigation clause.
readings.sourceQuote: Hierarchies (explained below).

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe 'Feature Hierarchies' FIRST - it is the label in the one topic that documents the click, and it is used by four further topics - and fall back to a contains-match on 'Hierarchies' only if the exact label is absent. Do not match on 'Hierarchies' first: it would also match unrelated menu text. CRITICAL AND SEPARATE FROM THE LABEL QUESTION: this entry is a SIBLING of Workflows in the left menu, not a child of it; a driver told to reach this page through a Workflows path WILL FAIL.
configContradictions.notes: Raised by the tables lens and the crosscut lens. Hypothesis: hierarchies-7f68a876.md is an editorially condensed overview that dropped the qualifier, rather than documenting a different UI - no corpus file states a UI change and no new-experience twin exists for any Feature Hierarchies file. The claim cannot be checked by menu-path comparison because 7f68a876's navigation clause uses U+00A0 separators and contains ZERO '>' characters; the fragment quoted here verifies but deliberately stops short of the separators and therefore does not itself carry the path. Both topics agree the parent chain is Administration > Invoice with no middle segment, so 'Invoice Processing Admin' is UNATTESTED for this page, not absent.

configContradictions.topic: The external setup guide that holds this page's real documentation is cited under five different titles, and none of the five is in this corpus.

readings.summary: Cited as the Shared: Feature Hierarchies Setup Guide - hierarchies only, Shared deliverable. The most common form.
readings.sourceQuote: Feature Hierarchies: The _Shared: Feature Hierarchies Setup Guide_

readings.summary: Cited as a COMBINED hierarchies-plus-group-configuration guide, singular Configuration.
readings.sourceQuote: _Shared: Feature Hierarchies and Group Configuration Setup Guide_

readings.summary: Cited as the same combined guide but with plural Configurations.
readings.sourceQuote: Shared: Feature Hierarchies and Group Configurations Setup Guide.

readings.summary: Cited under the Concur Invoice deliverable rather than Shared.
readings.sourceQuote: _Concur Invoice: Feature Hierarchies Setup Guide_

readings.summary: Cited as a hybrid naming two deliverables in one title.
readings.sourceQuote: refer to the Shared: Feature Hierarchies and Concur Invoice: Group Configurations Setup Guide.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: NO UI CONSEQUENCE - this is a documentation-sourcing consequence, and it is the ROOT CAUSE of this page's 'partial' coverage. When the graph is extended, search on the STEM 'Feature Hierarchies' plus 'Setup Guide' and accept any of the five titles; an exact-title search on any one of them will miss the other four. Do not assume the five names denote five different documents - assume ONE document until proven otherwise. Until it is ingested, no automation driver should expect field-level coverage of the Modify Hierarchy screen from this corpus.
configContradictions.notes: Raised by the tables lens and the crosscut lens; readings merged to the union of five titles. Hypothesis: one external guide, renamed and/or merged with the Group Configurations guide across SAP releases, with older cross-references left un-updated - a very common pattern in this corpus. Supporting circumstantial evidence: the guide is deferred to by name in at least eight in-corpus topics yet appears as a source file in none, and the two 'combined' variants differ only by a singular/plural s, which reads like drift rather than two real documents. appliesTo is EMPTY on purpose: this is a fact about the product's documentation set, not about any control on the page, and attaching it to a plausible neighbouring field would be false precision.

configContradictions.topic: Which activated feature makes the Authorized Approval Limits link appear - the Authorized Approver feature, or the Cost Object Approver feature. A driver has to know which flag to check before it goes looking for the link.

readings.summary: The Authorized Approvers guide thread gates the link on the AUTHORIZED APPROVER feature plus an Authorized Approver hierarchy carrying at least one level in addition to Global, and names no other feature anywhere in the topic.
readings.sourceQuote: If the Authorized Approver feature is activated and the company's Authorized Approver hierarchy has at least one level (in addition to Global), then the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section in Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.

readings.summary: The Cost Object Approval guide thread gates the SAME link on the COST OBJECT APPROVER feature instead - a different feature, activated at a different step of a different configuration sequence, and it leads with that condition as its opening sentence.
readings.sourceQuote: When the Cost Object Approver feature is activated, the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Settings section in User Administration.

readings.summary: Yet that same Cost Object Approval topic ALSO carries the Authorized-Approver-plus-hierarchy condition in its own Note, so this one file internally requires BOTH named features while the other file names only one. The corpus typo 'at least on level' is reproduced verbatim and is not a transcription slip on our side.
readings.sourceQuote: To view the Authorized Approval Limits link, you need to have activated the Authorized Approver feature and the company’s Authorized Approver hierarchy needs to have at least on level (in addition to Global).

readings.summary: Complicating the prerequisite further: the Cost Object Approval guide's own Configuration topic prescribes a DIFFERENTLY NAMED hierarchy as its Step 1 - a Cost Object Approver hierarchy - not the Authorized Approver hierarchy that both gate sentences above require. So it is not settled which hierarchy a driver must find a non-Global level in.
readings.sourceQuote: Step 1: Define the Concur Invoice Cost Object Approver hierarchy:

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not pick a side. Before treating the link's absence as a navigation failure, check BOTH feature flags plus the hierarchy precondition. Practical probe order, driven by corpus weight rather than by a resolution: the Authorized Approver feature plus a non-Global hierarchy level is asserted by BOTH primaries, so check it first (it is available on the built Workflows page as field.workflows.authorized_approver_feature_available_for_workflows); the Cost Object Approver feature is asserted by only one, so check it second, and check it FIRST if what is missing is specifically the Level control rather than the whole link. If the link still does not appear, do not conclude the page does not exist - conclude the provisioning is undetermined by the documentation and report that.
configContradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, offered as a hypothesis and never as a resolution: chapter provenance rather than a product disagreement. Each guide names its own chapter's feature as the headline gate because each is describing the rendering its own feature produces. Circumstantial support: 'Cost Object Approver feature' occurs in exactly two files corpus-wide - user-administration-8b167b96.md and configuration-8b3cce3f.md - and both belong to the Cost Object Approval guide thread (rev-history root cost-object-approval-8b3d1e0f.md, Step 4 sibling step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-82481079.md), while user-administrator-fcfd570c.md belongs to the Authorized Approvers guide thread (Step 4 sibling step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md). The corpus never states this reconciliation, so it stays open. A second, equally unproven reading is that the two features produce two different renderings of one link, which would make the visibility rule genuinely provisioning-dependent and would mean no single correct list exists to find. MERGED from three lens records (crosscut, procedure) that reported the same disagreement; readings deduplicated on (sourceFile, sourceQuote) and the fourth reading added from an independent read of the Cost Object Approval guide's Configuration topic.

configContradictions.topic: Whether a Level control exists on this surface at all - one topic tells the administrator to select a level in this window, another states outright that levels cannot be added through User Administration.

readings.summary: The Cost Object Approval guide's User Administration topic puts a Level control on the right side of this window, as the level branch of the same step-3 choice that offers the currency-and-amount pair.
readings.sourceQuote: For level-based cost object approval, select a level.

readings.summary: The same topic attests the control a SECOND time, independently, by naming it as one of two completable areas of this window in its precedence rule - so the Level field is not a one-sentence mention.
readings.sourceQuote: If you complete both areas in this window—the Approval Limit area and the Level field—Concur Invoice will use the one that applies to your configuration and ignore the other.

readings.summary: The Workflows level-filter topic denies it flatly: levels cannot be added to approvers through User Administration at all.
readings.sourceQuote: Levels cannot be added to approvers via User Administration.

readings.summary: The same passage enumerates the surfaces that CAN take a level - the Employee Import and the Workflows Authorized Approver list - excluding this window by omission as well as by the explicit prohibition.
readings.sourceQuote: The levels can be added to users via the Employee Import or the Authorized Approver list (Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Authorized Approver tab).

readings.summary: A third attestation muddies rather than settles it: the Authorized Approvers guide has the administrator selecting a level on the LEFT side of this same window. Whether that is the hierarchy-section selector or an approver level is not stated, so it cannot be counted as a clean vote for either side - but it does mean a level-shaped selection demonstrably occurs on this surface.
readings.sourceQuote: On the left side, the administrator selects the appropriate level in the hierarchy.

readings.summary: The Authorized Approvers overview enumerates only TWO authority kinds for an authorized approver - limit and exception - with no level among them, which is evidence that "level" is not an authorized-approver authority at all on this surface.
readings.sourceQuote: An authorized approver can have limit approval, exception approval, or both.

readings.summary: A second topic in the same guide family enumerates THREE authority kinds and DOES include level, directly disagreeing with the overview about whether level is an authorized-approver authority.
readings.sourceQuote: Authorized approvers will have limit, level, and/or exception approval and are affected by the authorized approver hierarchy.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do NOT resolve this in either direction and do not treat the two Level controls as interchangeable targets for one driver action. Treat the Level control on this window as PRESENT-BUT-UNCERTAIN: locate the Approval Limit area first, then probe for a Level control, and if it is absent record that as an expected outcome rather than a failed step - aae69350 predicts its absence. To set a WORKFLOW-STEP filter level, do not attempt it here: go to the built Workflows page (Administration > Invoice > Workflows), whose Authorized Approvers > Authorized Approver List tab carries field.workflows.authorized-approver-level, or use the employee import record type 720. To set a LEVEL-BASED COST OBJECT approval level, this window is the only surface the corpus offers; if the control is not rendered, the cost object configuration is limit-based and the Level half does not apply. Never present a level found here as the same value as field.workflows.authorized-approver-level.
configContradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, stated as a hypothesis and not adopted as a resolution: these are TWO DIFFERENT VALUES SHARING ONE ENGLISH LABEL, carried on two different employee-import record structures and belonging to two differently-named hierarchies. The level-based COST OBJECT approval level travels on record set 710 (employee-import-e28f2294.md, 'For the Limit hierarchy type, you will use the 710 Cost Object Approver record set...'), feeding the Cost Object Approver hierarchy that configuration-8b3cce3f.md defines in its Step 1. The authorized-approver WORKFLOW-STEP filter level travels on record type 720 (step-2-assign-the-level-to-the-approver-d8bf669c.md), feeding the Authorized Approver Hierarchy. The 720-versus-710 split is the concrete circumstantial evidence and the two topics sit in different guide threads (aae69350 in Authorized Approvers, 8b167b96 in Cost Object Approval), but no topic in this corpus states the reconciliation, so it stays open. Naming consequence already applied by the roster: the control on this window is named cost_object_approval_level precisely so it can never be confused with the built field.workflows.authorized-approver-level, which this run does not re-home and does not touch. MERGED from three lens records (crosscut, procedure, tables) reporting the same disagreement; readings deduplicated on (sourceFile, sourceQuote), with the second and fifth readings added from a direct re-read of the two primaries. CRITIC-ADDED 2026-09-01, AFTER THE ADVERSARIAL REFUTERS RAN. Quote grep -F verified. TWO FURTHER READINGS ADDED: the corpus does not agree with itself about whether "level" is an authorized-approver authority at all - authorized-approvers-overview-8b3bd2d0.md enumerates two kinds (limit, exception) and authorized-approvers-8b3ab7ad.md enumerates three (limit, level, exception). That widens this from a two-file disagreement about one control to a four-file disagreement about whether the concept belongs to this feature. Still NOT reconciled.

configContradictions.topic: How many acts it takes to configure an UNLIMITED approval amount on this window - clear the amount alone, or clear both the currency and the amount.

readings.summary: Describing THIS window, the Cost Object Approval guide states a ONE-act recipe: leave the amount blank. The currency is not mentioned at all.
readings.sourceQuote: For an unlimited approval amount, leave blank (null).

readings.summary: The surface-agnostic topic likewise states a single act - a null limit amount yields unlimited approval - and likewise says nothing about the currency.
readings.sourceQuote: When configuring the approver, a limit amount of null will result in an unlimited approval/no limit approval amount.

readings.summary: The Workflows sibling surface requires TWO acts - clear the currency AND leave the amount blank. This file is cited as BOUNDARY EVIDENCE about a different page, never as a source for a control on this one: its own click path is Administration > Invoice > Workflows and all four of its field rows are already built on the Workflows page.
readings.sourceQuote: If they are to have unlimited approval, set to no approval limit currency, and leave the approval limit amount blank.

readings.summary: The employee import record set pulls in the opposite direction from the one-act reading by making the currency conditionally REQUIRED whenever an amount is used - which leaves open what the currency should hold when the amount is deliberately null.
readings.sourceQuote: If Approval Limit is used, then this is required.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: On THIS window, clear the Amount and change nothing else - that is what both topics describing this surface say. Do NOT import the Workflows two-act recipe on the assumption the two surfaces behave identically. Whether the currency must ALSO be cleared here is UNDETERMINED BY THE DOCUMENTATION; if the save is rejected or the saved result reads as limited, additionally clearing the currency is the documented fallback for the sibling surface, but it must be logged as an observation, not executed as the documented procedure. Resolving it for certain would require a live tenant, which is out of bounds for a blind build. Separately and NOT part of this disagreement, a driver must never treat a blank amount as 'unset': blank means UNLIMITED, so a driver that leaves the amount empty because it had no value to write configures the exact opposite of a restriction. Zero, not blank, is the way to place an approver in the chain with no signing authority, and the zero semantics are uniform across every attestation.
configContradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, unproven either way: the difference may be surface-real (the Workflows New Authorized Approver form exposes a currency selector that must be explicitly emptied, while this window's Approval Limit area may not) or it may be a simple omission in the Cost Object Approval guide's much shorter procedure. Nothing in the corpus decides it, and no third file breaks the tie - 9d98b489 is surface-agnostic and sides with the one-act form only by silence about the currency. BOUNDARY NOTE, deliberate: the Workflows page already carries a sibling control for the same underlying value, field.workflows.authorized-approver-approval-limit, and it already records both the zero and the null semantics and already cites 9d98b489. Nothing here re-homes it and nothing here mints a fifth 'Approval Limit'. What is genuinely open on this surface is only the CURRENCY half of the recipe. MERGED from three lens records (crosscut, procedure, tables) that reported this disagreement against three different field names; homed on approval_limit_amount, the branch-B amount control on the roster, with the currency control approval_limit_currency_window implicated by the same open question.

configContradictions.topic: The name of the host section inside User Administration that holds the Authorized Approval Limits link drifts three ways across the corpus - and two of the three forms occur inside a single file.

readings.summary: Singular 'Setting' - the form attached to the branch-conditional sentence that actually describes this link. It occurs in exactly one file corpus-wide.
readings.sourceQuote: the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section in Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.

readings.summary: Plural 'Invoices Settings' - the second primary's own procedure step, the sentence a driver would follow to click the link.
readings.sourceQuote: In the Expense and Invoices Settings section of User Administration, click the Authorized Approval Limits link.

readings.summary: The SAME file writes the corpus-majority singular 'Expense and Invoice Settings' in its own opening summary, so the drift is inside one topic and not only between topics.
readings.sourceQuote: User Administration enables assignment of authorized approval limits for cost object approvers in Expense and Invoice Settings

readings.summary: Singular 'Invoice Settings' - the corpus-majority form, used from tools-guides to name the same region of the same user record for an unrelated control, which is evidence the majority form names the live section rather than being a local slip.
readings.sourceQuote: Under Expense and Invoice Settings, select the named vendor group from the list.

readings.summary: The majority form is confirmed to name a region of the User Details page populated by employee form fields, tying all three variants to one physical section rather than to three different places.
readings.sourceQuote: Employee Fields: Used by the Expense and Invoice Settings section of the User Details page.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not reconcile, and do not hard-match one literal string and fail. A driver searching the rendered page for the section header must accept all three forms, probing in corpus-weight order: 'Expense and Invoice Settings' FIRST, then 'Expense and Invoices Settings', then 'Expense and Invoices Setting'. Better still, match on the link text 'Authorized Approval Limits' - stable across every attestation in the corpus - and treat the section header as a locality hint only. Record the literal header text actually seen so later steps reuse the observed string rather than a guessed one.
configContradictions.notes: CORPUS WEIGHT, measured rather than assumed: grep -rlF over BOTH guide directories returns 'Expense and Invoice Settings' in six files (assigning-the-approver-for-the-purchase-request-user-20294611.md, fields-overview-5e3daf7c.md, set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md, user-administration-8b167b96.md, tools-guides/step-6-select-the-vendor-access-group-for-the-user-bb58ded2.md, tools-guides/step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md), 'Expense and Invoices Settings' in exactly one (user-administration-8b167b96.md), and 'Expense and Invoices Setting section' in exactly one (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md). HYPOTHESIS: the two 'Invoices' variants are typos local to the Authorized Approvers and Cost Object Approval guide threads respectively, and the live UI most likely reads 'Expense and Invoice Settings'. Unproven - a blind build cannot check the rendered UI, and singular/plural drift is exactly the kind of defect SAP guides carry for years. The intra-file evidence (reading 3 against reading 2, same file) is the strongest support for the typo reading, and is the reason the majority form is recommended as the first probe rather than as a coequal candidate.

configContradictions.topic: How deep the click path to this page actually is. The corpus renders the route to the containing User Administration surface at four different depths, twice inside one file, and this is the first page in this graph not reached under Administration > Invoice.

readings.summary: FOUR SEGMENTS. The sentence that describes this very link places it under Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.
readings.sourceQuote: the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section in Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.

readings.summary: The same file writes the same four-segment path a second time, for the branch-A check box on the same surface - so the long form is not a single slip.
readings.sourceQuote: the Authorized Approver check box appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section in Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.

readings.summary: TWO SEGMENTS, in that same file's own opening paragraph: the whole surface is reached at Administration > User Administration, with Company and Company Admin absent.
readings.sourceQuote: The settings that appear in User Administration (Administration > User Administration) differ depending on whether the configuration includes:

readings.summary: THREE SEGMENTS, and a different middle node: 'Company Administration' rather than 'Company Admin', with a Search & Select step between the surface and the section. Note that this file separates the segments with non-breaking spaces rather than the '>' character used elsewhere.
readings.sourceQuote: using Administration  Company Administration  User Administration (Search & Select)  Expense and Invoice Settings  Approvers.

readings.summary: A second, independent file corroborates the two-segment form for reaching the same section of the same user record, which means the short form is not unique to one writer.
readings.sourceQuote: accessing that user in Administration > User Administration. With the user loaded in the form, scroll to Expense and Invoice Settings.

readings.summary: ZERO SEGMENTS. The second primary names no click path at all, giving only the container name - so a driver reading only this topic has no route to follow.
readings.sourceQuote: the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Settings section in User Administration.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not reconcile these into one canonical path. Try the LONGER four-segment form first - Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration - because it is the form written by the only sentences that describe this link specifically, and because a driver that guesses short will stall on an intermediate menu it did not expect. If Company Admin is not present, fall back to Administration > Company > Company Administration, then to the bare two-segment Administration > User Administration. Assert on arrival at the User Administration surface with an employee record loaded, never on the exact menu wording. Two further facts that are NOT in dispute and must not be dropped while resolving the depth: the employee record must be loaded first (a Search & Select step precedes the section), and 'Invoice Processing Admin' appears in none of this page's documented paths and must never be offered as an alternate node here - this page is reached through Administration > Company, which makes it the first page in this graph not reached under Administration > Invoice.
configContradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: the short forms are abbreviations of the same route rather than a second entry point, and 'Company Admin' versus 'Company Administration' is menu-label drift of the kind this corpus carries throughout. Unproven, and deliberately not resolved: a site could legitimately render either, and menu labels are known to drift in this product.
